meta.title: Itch Atlas
meta.subtitle: Every problem on Razorpay's Fix My Itch, turned into a startup brief
meta.ratingNote: Platform problems are rated by the Fix My Itch score (0-100). Editorial picks are rated by a weighted founder score (0-100).

problems.title: How can travelers quickly find trusted doctors with clear costs in unfamiliar cities?
problems.description: International travelers and domestic tourists from other states who fall ill in unfamiliar cities don't know which hospitals or clinics to visit, whether doctors speak their language, or what treatment costs to expect, and they need dedicated tourist medical assistance helplines connecting them with verified English-speaking healthcare providers.
problems.who: International and out-of-state travellers who fall ill in a city they do not know.
problems.pitch: A traveller medical helpline that finds a verified, English-speaking doctor nearby with the cost stated before the visit.

how: Build a verified provider network with language, speciality, price range and insurance acceptance.
Run a WhatsApp/phone triage that books the right provider and sends an upfront cost estimate.
Add teleconsult as a first step and a follow-up check-in after treatment.
mvp: Provider network in three tourist cities
solution.model: Booking commission, insurer partnerships and a membership for frequent travellers.
solution.gtm: Hotels, travel insurers, tour operators and airport help desks.
solution.moat: Verified provider supply and language coverage.

problems.verdict: Falling ill abroad is a navigation problem before it is a medical one.

problems.title: Why don't homebuyers have standardized neighborhood quality data reports?
problems.description: Home buyers making multi-crore investment decisions lack comprehensive, data-driven information about neighborhood characteristics like school quality, crime statistics, air quality indices, water availability, power outage frequency, and future infrastructure plans that would inform purchasing choices beyond individual property inspection.
problems.who: Homebuyers choosing between projects with glossy brochures and no comparable data.
problems.pitch: A standard report on schools, crime, air, water, power and commute for any neighbourhood — before you commit a crore.

how: Combine public data (AQI, crime, water quality, outages, infrastructure plans) with on-ground audits and resident surveys.
Score each locality on eight dimensions and publish a comparable report with sources and confidence levels.
Sell reports to buyers and licence the data to developers, brokers and home-loan lenders.
mvp: Reports for 50 localities in one city
solution.model: Per-report fee, developer licences and lender API access.
solution.gtm: SEO on locality comparisons, broker partnerships, and lender risk teams.
solution.moat: Longitudinal locality data and an audit methodology.

problems.verdict: A ₹1 crore decision deserves better than a brochure.

problems.title: Why don’t apartments use QR gates for visitor parking management?
problems.description: Society residents constantly clash over visitor parking management because guests occupy limited parking spots for hours without proper permits, causing inconvenience to owners who find their own spaces blocked, yet societies lack digital permit systems, automated barriers, or QR-code-based temporary access controls.
problems.who: Housing societies with chronic visitor-parking clashes and blocked owner spots.
problems.pitch: Time-limited QR permits for visitor parking, approved by the resident and enforced at the gate.

how: Let residents issue a QR permit for a guest with a vehicle number and expiry time.
Scan at the gate, log entry/exit, and alert security when a vehicle overstays.
Integrate with boom barriers and add a tow-reminder workflow for unauthorised parking.
mvp: Resident permit app and gate scanner
solution.model: Per-flat monthly SaaS plus barrier hardware margin.
solution.gtm: Society committees and security agencies; start with 20 large societies.
solution.moat: Society contracts and gate hardware integration.

problems.verdict: Visitor parking is a permissions problem wearing a traffic costume.

problems.title: Why can't shop owners create websites without coding knowledge?
problems.description: Small retail shop owners wanting basic online presence to display products, hours, and contact information cannot use complex website builders requiring coding knowledge, design skills, or content structure planning, and they need voice-to-website AI tools that convert natural speech descriptions into functional storefronts.
problems.who: Kirana and boutique owners with no time, design skill or budget for a website.
problems.pitch: Speak your shop details and get a working storefront with catalogue, hours, location and WhatsApp ordering.

how: Use a voice-guided interview in the shopkeeper's language to capture products, prices, hours and photos.
Generate a mobile-first storefront with WhatsApp checkout, UPI details and Google Maps directions.
Add a repeat-order list and festival offer banner the owner can update by voice.
solution.model: Freemium storefront with a paid custom domain and catalogue sync.
solution.gtm: Distributor vans, local shop associations and a referral scheme for shopkeepers.
solution.moat: Local-language onboarding and merchant distribution.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr SME website and commerce tools

problems.verdict: The shopkeeper will not learn a builder; the builder must learn the shopkeeper.

problems.title: Why aren’t office shuttles dynamically routed based on real-time employee demand?
problems.description: Corporate employees commuting to business parks and IT campuses waste significant time waiting for scheduled company shuttles that run on fixed routes without demand-responsive scheduling, and they need on-demand van pooling apps that dynamically route vehicles based on real-time passenger requests.
problems.who: Business-park employees waiting 25 minutes for a half-empty shuttle; employers paying for unused seats.
problems.pitch: Demand-responsive office shuttles that route around who actually booked today, not a fixed route drawn two years ago.

how: Let employees request a seat by 4 pm for the next day, then optimise routes and departure times from the bookings.
Track occupancy and arrival performance, and re-plan routes weekly as teams shift to hybrid schedules.
Bill the employer per occupied seat and report cost per commute against the old fixed contract.
solution.model: Per-seat monthly fee plus a per-route optimisation fee.
solution.gtm: Business-park facility managers and large IT campuses; pilot on two routes.
solution.moat: Demand data and multi-tenant density in a park.

problems.verdict: Fixed routes are a scheduling habit that hybrid work has made expensive.

problems.title: Why is booking cargo vehicles harder than passenger transport?
problems.description: Consumers needing to transport single pieces of furniture, appliances, or bulk purchases across the city cannot easily book small cargo tempos or pickup trucks on-demand through apps like Uber, forcing them to negotiate with unorganized tempo drivers at inflated prices with no fare transparency or digital convenience.
problems.who: Consumers and small businesses moving single pieces of furniture or appliances across a city.
problems.pitch: Book a mini-truck for one sofa in 90 seconds, with a fare based on distance, loading and floor — not a negotiation.

how: Standardise vehicle classes (pickup, tempo, 1-tonne) with an upfront fare for distance, loading help and floor count.
Verify drivers and vehicles, track the trip, and add damage cover up to ₹25,000 per booking.
Schedule same-day slots and let the driver photograph the item at pickup and drop.
solution.model: 18–22% commission per trip plus a subscription for small businesses.
solution.gtm: Furniture stores, appliance retailers and moving-adjacent searches.
solution.moat: Driver density and a transparent fare engine that ends haggling.

problems.verdict: Cargo is where ride-hailing was in 2014 — same playbook, different load.

problems.title: Why do medicine prices vary wildly across pharmacy chains?
problems.description: Consumers discover the same prescription medicines are priced dramatically differently across pharmacy chains, with variations of 30-50% between retailers for identical drugs and dosages, because there is no transparent price comparison app allowing patients to find the most affordable nearby source before purchasing.
problems.who: Patients paying 30–50% more for the same molecule at the next pharmacy.
problems.pitch: Compare the real price of the same medicine across nearby pharmacies, with generic equivalents and expiry-aware stock.

how: Collect pharmacy-level prices through store partnerships and customer-submitted bills, normalised by brand, strength and pack.
Show the cheapest nearby options plus equivalent generics with the same salt composition.
Let users reserve for pickup and upload the bill to keep prices current.
mvp: Price comparison for 5,000 SKUs in one city
solution.model: Pharmacy referral fees, sponsored listings and a price-data API.
solution.gtm: Chronic-care patient groups, clinic pharmacies and neighbourhood pharmacy chains.
solution.moat: Crowdsourced price data at pack level.

problems.verdict: Drug prices are not secret; they are just not compared.

problems.title: Why do people struggle to track where their money goes each month?
problems.description: Individuals lose control over spending because transactions are scattered across UPI apps, cards, wallets, and subscriptions, with no single, simple view of everyday expenses in plain language.
problems.who: Salaried users whose money disappears across four apps and a credit card.
problems.pitch: One plain-language view of spending across UPI, cards and wallets, with subscriptions spotted and a monthly review that takes five minutes.

how: Use the Account Aggregator framework to pull bank, card and wallet transactions into one ledger.
Clean merchant names into recognisable labels and auto-detect subscriptions and recurring bills.
Send a weekly five-line summary with one specific saving action, not a dashboard to explore.
solution.model: Freemium subscription; anonymised spend-insight partnerships.
solution.gtm: Personal-finance creators and a free 'where did my salary go' audit.
solution.moat: Merchant-label data and a habit-forming weekly summary.

problems.verdict: A dashboard is not a habit; a weekly nudge is.

problems.title: Why is hotel and café WiFi unreliable for travelers?
problems.description: Travelers are misled by “high-speed WiFi” claims because connectivity quality is rarely measured or verified, leaving remote workers and tourists without dependable internet access when they need it most.
problems.who: Remote workers and travellers choosing a stay partly on connectivity.
problems.pitch: Measured, verified WiFi speed at hotels and cafés — tested by guests, not claimed by marketing.

how: Run an automatic speed and latency test when a guest joins the network, with a 20-second opt-in.
Publish a verified WiFi score per property and per area (room, lobby, café), updated weekly.
Licence the badge and feed to booking sites and hotels that want to prove their claim.
solution.model: Venue certification fees, booking affiliate revenue and a data API.
solution.gtm: Digital-nomad communities, boutique hotels and co-working cafés.
solution.moat: Longitudinal measurement data by venue.

problems.verdict: Speed claims are cheap; a timestamped test is not.

problems.title: Why don't apartments have smart water sub-meters?
problems.description: Apartment residents overpay for water because buildings lack affordable smart sub-meters, forcing societies to split bills equally regardless of actual consumption and removing incentives for conservation.
problems.who: Societies splitting water bills equally while a few flats consume most of it.
problems.pitch: Affordable per-flat water sub-meters with app billing and leak alerts, retrofitted without rewiring the building.

how: Install clamp-on or inline smart meters per flat with a low-power radio gateway per floor.
Generate consumption-based bills and flag abnormal usage or a continuous-flow leak within hours.
Finance the hardware through a per-flat monthly fee and share savings with the society.
solution.model: Hardware plus a per-flat SaaS fee; water-saving performance share.
solution.gtm: Water-stressed cities and large societies with high tanker costs.
solution.moat: Installation base and consumption benchmarks.

problems.verdict: You cannot conserve what you do not measure.

problems.title: Why do factory workers lack affordable first-mile transport to factory jobs?
problems.description: Daily wage laborers and factory shift workers in industrial areas lack affordable first-mile and last-mile connectivity from residential areas to manufacturing plants, wasting 2-3 hours daily on exhausting walks, and companies need dedicated micro-transit systems that provide subsidized transportation for blue-collar employees.
problems.who: Factory workers losing 2–3 hours daily; plant HR teams battling absenteeism and attrition.
problems.pitch: Employer-paid micro-transit that collects factory workers from their neighbourhoods and gets them home after shift.

how: Cluster worker home addresses and build dynamic 12–16 seat routes per shift, with a driver app and seat manifest.
Track boarding by QR and alert HR to no-shows; adjust routes weekly as worker addresses change.
Bill the employer per seat per month, with a subsidy split that can include the worker.
mvp: Driver app with manifest and boarding scan
solution.model: Per-seat monthly contracts with industrial plants; own or partner fleet.
solution.gtm: Industrial estates and plant HR heads; pilot on one shift and prove attendance gains.
solution.moat: Route data and multi-plant density that lowers cost per seat.

problems.verdict: The buyer is the factory, the user is the worker, and the metric is attendance.

problems.title: Why are half of rental listings fake broker clickbait?
problems.description: Prospective tenants searching for rental homes discover that half of attractive listings on property portals are fraudulent advertisements posted by brokers using fake photos, unavailable properties, or significantly different actual offerings designed purely to capture contact information and generate commission-based inquiries.
problems.who: Tenants wasting weekends on bait listings and brokers who 'just missed' the flat.
problems.pitch: Rental listings that are verified available, owner-authorised and audited — with a photo of the actual flat today.

how: Require owner verification via Aadhaar-linked OTP and a property document check before a listing goes live.
Send a field agent to capture a timestamped video walkthrough and confirm availability within 72 hours.
Guarantee the listing: if the flat is unavailable or materially different, the tenant gets ₹500 and the broker is delisted.
solution.model: Listing fee from owners plus a tenant subscription for early access.
solution.gtm: Start in two high-churn rental corridors; publish a fake-listing takedown counter.
solution.moat: Verified supply and audit operations.

problems.verdict: Verification is the entire product; everything else is a listing site.

problems.title: How do beauty buyers verify product authenticity on e-commerce?
problems.description: Consumers purchasing skincare and cosmetics through online marketplaces live in fear of receiving counterfeit products, expired inventory, or tampered-with items because platforms lack robust batch verification systems, holographic authentication seals, or manufacturing date transparency that would guarantee genuine product origins.
problems.who: Beauty and personal-care buyers on marketplaces who fear counterfeits.
problems.pitch: Scan the batch code before you buy — authenticity, expiry and manufacturer verified at the unit level.

how: Issue serialised QR/batch codes to brands at packaging, with a scan ledger that detects duplicates and out-of-territory stock.
Let shoppers scan in-app or via the e-commerce listing to see authenticity, manufacture and expiry details.
Alert brands to suspicious scan clusters and provide a takedown evidence pack.
solution.model: Per-code fee, brand SaaS, and verification-as-a-service for marketplaces.
solution.gtm: Start with 10 indie beauty brands sold on marketplaces; use counterfeit seizures as proof.
solution.moat: Brand code inventory and a scan network that gets smarter with volume.

market.tam: ₹15,000 Cr beauty e-commerce; authentication a trust layer

problems.verdict: If a buyer can verify one scan, the counterfeit economy loses its edge.

problems.title: How do buyers discover dampness after moving into homes?
problems.description: Home purchasers investing life savings discover hidden water seepage, structural cracks, termite damage, or foundation issues within weeks of possession because pre-purchase home inspections using thermal imaging, moisture meters, and structural engineering assessments are not standard practice in Indian real estate transactions.
problems.who: Buyers spending life savings on a home with hidden damp and termite damage.
problems.pitch: A pre-purchase moisture, thermal and structural inspection that finds seepage before the keys change hands.

how: Run a standard 90-minute inspection with thermal imaging, moisture meters and a structural checklist.
Produce a report with annotated images, severity, likely cause and a repair cost range.
Offer a 12-month re-inspection guarantee and a repair-partner quote.
solution.model: Per-inspection fee plus repair partner commissions.
solution.price: ₹4,999–₹9,999 per home; ₹1,999 for a single-room check.
solution.gtm: Home-loan lenders, buyer agents and resale listings; partner with banks for pre-disbursement checks.
solution.moat: Inspection data and lender trust.

risks: Buyers skip inspections to save money
problems.verdict: The most expensive defect is the one you meet after possession.

problems.title: Why do fresh graduates lack practical coding skills despite strong academic performance?
problems.description: Companies hiring fresh graduates discover candidates possess theoretical knowledge and good academic scores but cannot solve basic programming problems, debug code, or apply concepts practically because college curricula rely on theoretical lectures without providing hands-on industry-simulation labs or real-world project experience.
problems.who: Final-year students and fresh graduates with strong marks but no working portfolio.
problems.pitch: A coding school built around shipping real software: industry-simulation labs, code review and debugging drills instead of lecture notes.

how: Replace syllabus chapters with 12 week-long simulations: a payments bug, a slow query, a broken deploy, each with tests and a reviewer.
Require every learner to maintain a public repo with CI, tests and a written post-mortem for each project.
Grade on debugging and code review, then route top performers to hiring partners who interview from the repo.
mvp: Three simulation tracks with automated tests
Public portfolio and verified skill report
solution.model: Income-share or fixed-fee bootcamp, plus college licensing for the labs.
solution.gtm: College placement cells, coding communities, and a free 'debug this repo' challenge as the top of funnel.
solution.moat: A reviewed project corpus and employer trust in the skill signal.

risks: Placement outcomes depend on the market

market.tam: ₹25,000 Cr higher-ed and upskilling; employability a ₹4,000 Cr slice

problems.verdict: Employers do not buy degrees; they buy evidence of work.

problems.title: Why can’t NRIs remotely secure vacant properties with real-time monitoring and alerts?
problems.description: Non-resident Indians maintaining vacant properties in their hometowns live with constant anxiety about unauthorized occupancy, illegal construction, or squatter occupation during prolonged absences because traditional property management services don't provide smart home security systems, video monitoring, or biometric access controls with real-time alerts.
problems.who: NRI owners of vacant homes worried about squatters, illegal construction and burst pipes.
problems.pitch: Remote property guardianship for NRIs: sensors, cameras, periodic visits and a local escalation team when something moves.

how: Install a cellular-connected sensor kit (door, motion, water, power) that works without home broadband.
Schedule monthly physical visits with a photo report, and keep a document vault for taxes and utilities.
Escalate to a verified local representative and lawyer when an alert needs a physical response.
solution.model: Annual subscription plus hardware and visit fees.
solution.gtm: NRI associations, property lawyers and wealth managers.
solution.moat: Local response networks across cities and trust with absent owners.

problems.verdict: Absence is the vulnerability; presence is the product.

problems.title: How do property ads lie about commute times?
problems.description: Prospective home buyers and renters discover that real estate marketing claims like "5 minutes from metro" are wildly inaccurate because they measure straight-line distances on maps rather than actual peak-hour walking time accounting for traffic signals, crowded sidewalks, and infrastructure obstacles.
problems.who: Buyers and renters misled by '5 minutes from metro' claims.
problems.pitch: Peak-hour door-to-door commute times measured from real trips, not straight-line map distances.

how: Compute commute time to major employment hubs using transit, driving and walking legs at 8–10 am, not off-peak.
Publish a commute score per listing with the route and time band, and audit claims against it.
Licence the API to portals and brokers, and let buyers compare two homes by commute.
solution.model: Portal and developer licences; consumer premium reports.
solution.gtm: Consumer advocate PR, portal partnerships and relocation companies.
solution.moat: Peak-hour trip data by corridor.

problems.verdict: Distance sells homes; commute is what buyers actually live with.

problems.title: Why are college choices influenced by referral fees instead of student aptitude?
problems.description: High school graduates receive biased college recommendations from counseling agencies and education consultants who prioritize their own commission structures over student aptitude, interests, or career goals, steering confused teenagers toward expensive private institutions that pay the highest referral fees.
problems.who: Class 12 students and parents choosing between expensive private colleges with hidden incentives.
problems.pitch: Fee-only college advisory with transparent pricing, aptitude matching and published outcome data — no referral commissions.

how: Build a college dataset with real fees, placement rates, median salaries and accreditation status, normalised across institutions.
Run an aptitude and constraint interview, then produce three tiers of options with total cost and likely outcomes.
Charge families a flat fee and publish a 'no commission' pledge, with a refund if the student's top choice is later found misrepresented.
mvp: College outcome database for two states
Five counsellors trained on the method
solution.model: Flat advisory fee; later, a B2B licence for schools and lenders.
solution.price: ₹4,999–₹14,999 per family; ₹2,500 for a group workshop.
solution.gtm: School counsellor partnerships, parent webinars, and SEO on 'which college should I choose'.
solution.moat: Outcome data and a reputation for refusing referral money.

problems.verdict: Neutral advice is a business model, not an ethics statement.

problems.title: Why don’t global learning platforms support high-quality regional language instruction?
problems.description: Exceptionally talented students from non-metro areas who are highly skilled in their fields cannot access elite global online courses, certification programs, or educational content from top institutions because these resources are exclusively available in English and haven't been localized into regional Indian languages.
problems.who: Talented non-metro students locked out of English-only global courseware.
problems.pitch: High-quality regional-language versions of elite courses, with local mentors and assessments — not machine-translated subtitles.

how: License 20 high-demand courses and rebuild them with native-language instructors, not just dubbing.
Localise examples, assessments and support, with a regional mentor available for doubt sessions.
Certify learners against the same assessment standard as the English version.
solution.model: Course licensing margin plus a subscription for mentor support.
solution.gtm: Regional YouTube educators, district-level study centres, and state skilling partnerships.
solution.moat: Licensed content and a native instructor bench.

market.tam: ₹18,000 Cr online learning; regional-language supply is thin

problems.verdict: English is not the barrier; English-only assessment is.

problems.title: How can small brands optimize digital ads within limited budgets?
problems.description: Small brands lose advertising spend because they lack the expertise and time to continuously optimize campaigns, making manual keyword tuning and budget allocation inefficient for low-budget Google Ads accounts.
problems.who: Small brands spending ₹50,000–₹3 lakh a month with no dedicated media buyer.
problems.pitch: An autopilot ad optimizer for small budgets: it reallocates spend daily and explains every change in one line.

how: Connect Google and Meta accounts, set a target CPA and a hard budget guardrail.
Reallocate budget across keywords, creatives and audiences daily, pausing anything that breaches the guardrail.
Send a weekly plain-language report with the three changes that mattered and the next experiment.
solution.model: Flat SaaS fee plus a small share of verified savings.
solution.gtm: D2C communities, agency overflow work and Shopify app listings.
solution.moat: Cross-account performance benchmarks for small budgets.

market.tam: ₹40,000 Cr digital ad spend; SMB slice underserved

problems.verdict: Small budgets fail from neglect, not from bad strategy.

problems.title: Why do daily commuters waste 90 minutes in traffic?
problems.description: Office goers in metros spend 1.5-2 hours each way commuting through congested routes. No carpooling culture exists. Company shuttles are limited. Public transport is overcrowded. Real-time traffic-based route optimization apps don't provide multi-modal alternatives. Commute time wastes 15-20 hours weekly.
problems.who: Metro commuters losing 15–20 hours a week to fragmented, unreliable routes.
problems.pitch: A peak-hour commute planner that combines metro, shuttle, bike and walking into one guaranteed itinerary — and pays you if it fails.

how: Model first/last-mile options against real peak-hour timings, crowding and reliability, not static schedules.
Offer a guaranteed arrival time on the recommended itinerary, with a cab credit if it slips by more than 15 minutes.
Add a carpool match for the last mile where transit does not reach.
solution.model: Subscription plus affiliate revenue from cab and bike partners.
solution.gtm: Corporate commute benefits and metro-station activation.
solution.moat: Peak-hour reliability data by corridor.

problems.verdict: Commuters do not need another map; they need a promise.

problems.title: How can companies eliminate unused SaaS subscriptions efficiently?
problems.description: Organizations accumulate wasteful spending on dozens of SaaS subscriptions with inactive user seats, forgotten trial conversions, and redundant tools purchased by different departments because finance teams lack centralized visibility into all software expenditures and automated alerts for license optimization opportunities.
problems.who: Finance and ops teams with 40 tools and no single owner of software spend.
problems.pitch: Find every SaaS tool, every unused seat and every auto-renewal — then cancel or renegotiate it in one click.

how: Connect email, cards and SSO logs to discover tools, seats, spend and last-login dates.
Score each subscription for utilisation and overlap, then generate a cancel or downgrade action plan.
Execute cancellations and renewal negotiations with vendor-specific playbooks and a savings report.
mvp: Discovery from email and card feeds
solution.model: SaaS fee plus a share of first-year savings.
solution.gtm: CFO and startup communities; offer a free spend audit as the wedge.
solution.moat: Vendor pricing and cancellation playbooks plus benchmark data.

risks: Customers cancel in-house after the audit
problems.verdict: Every unused seat is a subscription someone forgot to own.

problems.title: Why can't customers find verified plumbers for emergencies?
problems.description: Homeowners facing plumbing emergencies at night or weekends cannot find verified, trustworthy plumbers instantly. Local search results show unverified listings with no ratings or background checks. Emergency charges are inflated 2-3x. Service quality is unpredictable. No on-demand platform provides verified emergency plumbers with transparent pricing and instant availability.
problems.who: Homeowners with a burst pipe at 11 pm and no trusted plumber on call.
problems.pitch: A verified emergency plumber at your door in 60 minutes, with night pricing published before you confirm.

how: Build an on-call roster of verified plumbers per zone, with ID checks, insurance and a 60-minute SLA.
Publish fixed emergency call-out and common-repair prices; the customer approves before dispatch.
Stock a standard parts kit in each van and guarantee the repair for 30 days.
mvp: Fixed price card and dispatch app
solution.model: Call-out fee plus parts margin; annual home-plumbing membership.
solution.gtm: SEO on emergency plumbing queries, society noticeboards and security desks.
solution.moat: Night-time supply density and trust with housing societies.

problems.verdict: Emergencies are won by who answers at 11 pm.

problems.title: Why do shoppers visit stores only to find items unavailable?
problems.description: Consumers planning to purchase specific products from nearby retail stores frequently make wasted trips because they cannot check real-time shelf inventory online before leaving home, arriving at stores only to discover their desired items are sold out or not yet restocked.
problems.who: Shoppers making wasted trips; small retailers losing sales to 'out of stock' walkouts.
problems.pitch: Live shelf inventory from neighbourhood stores, so shoppers can check stock and reserve before leaving home.

how: Integrate with billing/POS systems and a lightweight stock-count app for stores without one.
Expose a consumer search by pincode with 'in stock now' confidence and a free 2-hour hold.
Track walk-in conversion for retailers so the integration pays for itself.
mvp: POS connectors for three billing systems
solution.model: Retailer SaaS per store plus promoted placement.
solution.gtm: Start with electronics and pharmacy where stock-outs hurt most; sell through distributor networks.
solution.moat: Store-level inventory data and POS integrations.

market.tam: ₹40 lakh+ kirana and specialty stores; retail software a ₹2,000 Cr market

problems.verdict: The data already exists at the counter — the product is making it searchable.

problems.title: Why can't SMEs negotiate favorable payment terms with large buyers?
problems.description: Small suppliers selling to large corporate buyers face one-sided payment terms of 60-90 days or longer, while needing to pay their own suppliers within 30 days. This creates working capital gaps forcing SMEs to take expensive short-term loans at 18-24% interest. Large buyers refuse to negotiate shorter payment cycles, knowing small suppliers are desperate for orders. No mechanism exists to standardize or enforce fair payment terms, leaving SMEs cash-starved despite having confirmed orders.
problems.who: SME suppliers selling to large corporates on 60–120 day payment cycles.
problems.pitch: Payment-term infrastructure that gives an SME supplier the leverage of a large buyer.

how: Benchmark payment terms by buyer and industry so a supplier knows what is normal before signing.
Offer buyer-backed reverse factoring: underwrite the receivable, not the SME, and settle in days for a small discount.
Automate e-invoicing, collection nudges and a dispute desk so cash does not stall on paperwork.
mvp: Two NBFC partners and 20 buyer programmes
solution.model: Factoring spread, supplier SaaS, benchmark subscription for larger suppliers.
solution.price: 0.5–1.5% per invoice financed. ₹4,999/month for the platform.
solution.gtm: Industry clusters such as auto components and textiles, CA networks and large-buyer supplier programmes.
solution.moat: Receivable performance data by buyer plus capital partnerships. Hard to bootstrap, valuable once live.

market.tam: ₹50 lakh Cr+ in B2B receivables, with MSME working capital as the wedge

problems.verdict: This is the highest-itch problem on the platform for a reason: cash flow is the SME's real product.

problems.title: How can consumers verify water purification in delivery cans?
problems.description: Households ordering 20-liter water cans from local suppliers cannot verify whether water is genuinely RO-purified or just filtered tap water. Suppliers claim RO purification but provide no proof. Testing water quality at home requires expensive TDS meters. Water-borne illnesses from impure delivered water are common. No tamper-proof purity verification seals or batch-level quality certificates exist for packaged drinking water delivery.
problems.who: Households drinking 20-litre cans with no proof the water was RO-purified.
problems.pitch: A tamper-evident seal and batch test certificate on every water can — scan it and see the actual lab result.

how: Seal every can at the plant with a numbered cap, and bind the batch to a lab test certificate.
Let customers scan the cap to see the plant, batch, test date and TDS/microbiology results.
Audit suppliers quarterly and publish a plant scorecard; replace suppliers that fail.
solution.model: Per-seal fee from water suppliers plus a consumer subscription for home testing.
solution.gtm: Apartment societies and water-supplier associations; lead with a public purity index.
solution.moat: Supplier audit data and society-level trust.

problems.verdict: Purity claims need a receipt.

problems.title: Why do migrant workers lose money on remittances?
problems.description: Workers overpay to send money home because remittance services hide fees within exchange rates and charges, preventing transparent comparison and fair pricing.
problems.who: Workers sending ₹10,000–₹30,000 home monthly and losing 3–6% to hidden spreads.
problems.pitch: True-cost remittance comparison and receipt tracking for migrant workers, in their language and on WhatsApp.

how: Compute the landed amount for every licensed channel, including the FX spread, fee and receiving-bank charges.
Let users send through the cheapest channel from the app and store a receipt with the exact rate and fee.
Add an agent-assisted mode at labour chowks for workers who cannot navigate apps.
mvp: WhatsApp send flow in three languages
solution.model: Referral commission from remittance partners plus a small convenience fee.
solution.gtm: Labour contractors, migrant worker unions, and WhatsApp groups in source districts.
solution.moat: Channel-cost data and worker trust in the source districts.

problems.verdict: Transparency is worth most to the people with the least.

problems.title: Why do patients lack tools to compare conflicting diagnoses confidently?
problems.description: Patients seeking second medical opinions for serious health conditions struggle to determine if conflicting diagnoses, contradictory treatment plans, or significantly different prescriptions from multiple doctors are due to legitimate medical complexity or potential misdiagnosis requiring further specialist consultation and diagnostic confirmation.
problems.who: Patients with serious conditions who receive contradictory advice and do not know whom to trust.
problems.pitch: A structured second opinion: your records, an independent specialist review, and a plain-language comparison of why the diagnoses differ.

how: Collect reports, imaging and prescriptions into a structured case file with a timeline of symptoms and tests.
Route to an independent specialist in the same field who reviews the file and answers a fixed question set.
Deliver a comparison memo: where the diagnoses diverge, what evidence is missing, and which test would settle it.
solution.model: Per-review fee, with hospital and insurer partnerships.
solution.gtm: Oncology and cardiology patient groups, insurer case management and hospital discharge desks.
solution.moat: A specialist panel and structured case outcomes.

problems.verdict: The second opinion is valuable because it is structured, not because it is second.

problems.title: Why is it so hard to find power outlets for devices while traveling?
problems.description: Travelers whose mobile phones die during sightseeing, shopping, or commuting face severe inconvenience because finding public electrical outlets for emergency charging is impossible, and they need widespread powerbank-sharing networks with kiosk pickup/drop-off systems similar to bike-sharing services.
problems.who: Travellers whose phone dies mid-sightseeing or between trains.
problems.pitch: A powerbank-sharing network at transit hubs and cafés — pick up when your phone dies, drop it at the next stop.

how: Place kiosks with 20–40 powerbanks at stations, airports and partner cafés, unlocked by QR.
Price by hours used and let users drop at any kiosk in the network.
Add a lost-device charge and a map of live kiosk inventory.
solution.model: Rental fees, kiosk advertising and café partnership revenue.
solution.gtm: Railway stations, airports, malls and café chains.
solution.moat: Kiosk density and a drop-anywhere network.

problems.verdict: A dead phone is the one travel emergency everyone has.

problems.title: How do small teams struggle with manual payroll calculations?
problems.description: Businesses employing fewer than 10 workers spend hours each month manually calculating employee salaries factoring in variable elements like paid leave, unpaid absences, overtime hours, and festival bonuses because payroll software is designed for larger organizations and doesn't offer one-click processing for tiny teams.
problems.who: Small business owners spending a weekend a month on salaries and PF/ESI.
problems.pitch: One-click payroll for teams under ten: attendance, leave, overtime, festival bonus and compliance in a single run.

how: Import attendance from a shared sheet or biometric device, then calculate salary, leave and overtime automatically.
Handle PF, ESI, TDS and payslips with a compliance calendar and challan reminders.
Pay salaries via bank/UPI in one batch and file the statutory returns from the same data.
solution.model: Per-employee monthly fee with a compliance add-on.
solution.gtm: CA firms, trade associations and small-business WhatsApp groups.
solution.moat: Compliance rules engine and CA distribution.

problems.verdict: Tiny teams need payroll to feel like sending a message, not filing a return.

problems.title: Why don’t people understand the insurance policies they buy?
problems.description: Policyholders make uninformed decisions because insurance documents are written in legal and technical language, obscuring exclusions and conditions that directly affect claim outcomes.
problems.who: Policyholders who discover exclusions only when they file a claim.
problems.pitch: Upload any policy and get a plain-language map of what is covered, what is excluded and what a claim will actually pay.

how: Parse the policy wording into a structured coverage table: events, limits, sub-limits, waiting periods and exclusions.
Show three claim scenarios with the actual payout maths, and flag gaps against the user's stated needs.
Offer a paid review with a licensed advisor and a claim-assistance pack when a claim is filed.
mvp: Policy parser for the top 10 insurers
solution.model: Per-report fee, advisor referral, and a subscription for annual policy reviews.
solution.gtm: SEO on policy-wordings, claims stories, and partnerships with claim-help firms.
solution.moat: A structured clause library across insurers and products.

market.tam: ₹9 lakh Cr insurance premiums; comprehension a trust wedge

problems.verdict: The claim is won or lost at the exclusions page.

problems.title: Why is scholarship information fragmented and inaccessible to low-income and rural students?
problems.description: Deserving students from economically weaker sections or remote areas remain unaware of available government scholarships, private grants, and financial aid opportunities because information is scattered across disconnected platforms, application processes are complex, and they lack mentors who can guide them through documentation requirements.
problems.who: Rural and low-income students who never hear about the money they qualify for.
problems.pitch: One verified scholarship database with eligibility matching, document checklists and a mentor who answers on WhatsApp.

how: Crawl and verify every central, state and private scholarship, then normalise eligibility into a filterable schema.
Match students to schemes, generate a document checklist and track deadlines with reminders.
Recruit verified mentors to review applications and run physical help desks in district colleges.
solution.model: CSR and foundation funding; college partnerships; no fee from students.
solution.price: Free to students; ₹2–5 lakh per district partnership.
solution.gtm: District colleges, state welfare boards and education NGOs.
solution.moat: Verified, structured scheme data and mentor coverage.

market.tam: ₹50,000 Cr+ scholarship disbursement; discovery is the bottleneck

problems.verdict: The money exists; the map does not.

problems.title: Why are mock tests and analytics inaccessible to low-income exam candidates?
problems.description: NEET, JEE, and competitive exam aspirants from economically disadvantaged backgrounds cannot afford premium coaching classes that provide extensive question banks, doubt-clearing support, and mock test series, leaving them relying solely on outdated textbooks without access to quality practice problems and performance analytics.
problems.who: NEET/JEE aspirants who cannot afford ₹15,000 test series.
problems.pitch: Sponsor-funded mock tests and analytics for low-income aspirants — free to the student, paid for by CSR and colleges.

how: Build a question bank and a full-length mock engine with topic-level analytics and a weak-area plan.
Fund it through CSR sponsorships and college partnerships, with sponsor branding kept away from question content.
Add offline test centres and a WhatsApp doubt line for students without steady internet.
solution.model: CSR grants and college licences; optional paid mentoring for those who want it.
solution.price: Free to students; ₹3–8 lakh annual CSR package.
solution.gtm: District education officers, NGO networks, and CSR foundations focused on education.
solution.moat: Sponsor relationships and a large aspirant dataset.

problems.verdict: Access is a funding design problem, not a pricing problem.

problems.title: Why do emergency rooms lack systems to prioritize critical patients instantly?
problems.description: Hospital emergency departments operate on chaotic first-come-first-serve protocols where critical patients wait behind less urgent cases because facilities lack AI-powered triage systems that can instantly assess vital signs, symptom severity, and medical urgency to prioritize life-threatening conditions over minor ailments.
problems.who: Emergency departments running first-come-first-serve; patients deteriorating in the waiting room.
problems.pitch: A triage support layer that scores arriving patients on vitals and symptoms so the sickest are seen first.

how: Capture vitals and a short symptom set at arrival, then compute an ESI-style acuity score with a clear escalation rule.
Show a live triage board to the clinical team with re-assessment timers for waiting patients.
Log door-to-doctor times and deterioration events for audit and quality reporting.
solution.model: Per-bed hospital SaaS plus implementation.
solution.gtm: Mid-sized private hospitals and trauma centres; start with one pilot ED.
solution.moat: Triage outcome data and clinical validation.

problems.verdict: The waiting room is where the next avoidable death hides.

problems.title: Why does investing feel intimidating to ordinary people?
problems.description: Retail investors avoid markets because investment platforms emphasize products and jargon instead of personal goals, making participation feel complex and risky. The investors have to self educate using online sources that leave them feeling under-confident and intimidated.
problems.who: First-time investors who freeze between 40 fund options and jargon.
problems.pitch: Investing explained through a goal, not a product — a human-guided plan with plain-language trade-offs and small SIPs.

how: Start with a goal interview (house, education, retirement) and convert it into a monthly number with a range of outcomes.
Recommend a three-fund portfolio and explain every choice in one sentence, with a human advisor available on call.
Show progress against the goal, not just returns, and nudge top-ups at salary dates.
mvp: Advisor call booking and progress view
solution.model: RIA fee on assets or a flat annual planning fee; no product commissions.
solution.gtm: Employer financial-wellness sessions, YouTube explainers, and referral from existing investors.
solution.moat: A fee-only advice brand and goal-outcome data.

market.tam: ₹40 lakh Cr mutual fund AUM; first-time investor segment underpenetrated

problems.verdict: People do not fear markets; they fear not understanding the next screen.

problems.title: Why do payment apps have confusing cashback terms?
problems.description: Users making payments see promotional offers like '10% cashback up to ₹100' but discover complex conditions in fine print - minimum transaction amounts, specific merchants only, first-time user restrictions, or bank-specific offers. Cashback promised at payment time often doesn't arrive. Terms like 'up to' mislead users into expecting more than they receive. No standardized, upfront clarity exists on exact cashback users will receive before confirming payment.
problems.who: Shoppers burned by '10% up to ₹100' offers that pay nothing.
problems.pitch: Before you pay, see the exact cashback you will get after every condition — then track whether it actually landed.

how: Parse offer terms into rules (minimum spend, merchant list, cap, first-time-only) and compute the expected payout for this specific transaction.
Show a pre-payment verdict and log the promise so the user can claim later.
Auto-detect missing cashback from SMS/email and generate a claim with the offer evidence.
solution.model: Affiliate revenue plus a premium claims service.
solution.gtm: Deal communities and UPI app partnerships; publish a 'cashback that never arrived' report.
solution.moat: Offer-term data and claim outcomes.

problems.verdict: The fine print is the product.

problems.title: How do parents find trustworthy evening childcare for short hours?
problems.description: Professional parents working late shifts or attending evening events face severe childcare gaps because they cannot easily locate verified, trustworthy caregivers available for short-duration evening sessions without committing to expensive monthly nanny services or imposing on already-exhausted grandparents.
problems.who: Dual-income parents with late shifts, school events or evening plans, and no grandparent backup.
problems.pitch: Verified evening childcare by the hour, with police checks, insurance and a two-hour minimum.

how: Recruit caregivers with verified ID, police verification, reference checks and a paediatric first-aid certificate.
Offer 2–5 hour evening slots with check-in/check-out photos, a activity log and live arrival tracking.
Carry accident insurance per session and run a replacement guarantee if a sitter cancels.
solution.model: Commission per booking plus a monthly family membership for priority slots.
solution.gtm: Apartment communities, preschool parent groups and corporate HR benefits.
solution.moat: Local verified supply and trust density; parents rebook the same sitter.

market.tam: ₹8,000 Cr urban childcare, with evening gaps underserved

problems.verdict: Trust is expensive to build and therefore valuable once built.

problems.title: Why do drivers circle markets for 20 minutes finding parking?
problems.description: Shoppers and visitors driving to popular commercial areas and crowded markets waste significant time circling streets looking for available parking spots, creating traffic congestion and pollution, because there is no system allowing them to view real-time parking availability or reserve spaces in advance.
problems.who: Shoppers and visitors to dense commercial areas who lose 20 minutes circling.
problems.pitch: See and reserve a real parking spot before you enter a crowded market, using lots that already exist.

how: Onboard private lots, society basements and temple/market parking with an attendant app that updates occupancy.
Show live availability by area and let drivers reserve a 30-minute hold with a small fee.
Price dynamically by demand and share revenue with the lot owner.
solution.model: Booking fee commission plus SaaS for lot owners.
solution.gtm: Start with three high-congestion market clusters; partner with merchant associations who want footfall.
solution.moat: Exclusive lot inventory in dense zones — the supply side is the moat.

problems.verdict: Parking is a supply-contract business disguised as an app.

problems.title: Why do quick-delivery apps send bruised fruits and vegetables?
problems.description: Customers ordering from ultra-fast delivery services prioritizing speed over quality routinely receive damaged fruits, bruised vegetables, and crushed packaged goods because warehouse pickers rush through selection and delivery partners prioritize completion times over careful product handling and temperature-controlled transportation.
problems.who: Quick-commerce shoppers who pay a premium and receive bruised produce.
problems.pitch: Quality-graded produce for quick commerce, with a pack-side photo and a no-questions refund if the grade is missed.

how: Grade produce at the dark store into A/B/C with a size, firmness and blemish standard, and photograph each packed bag.
Route A-grade to express orders, B-grade to discounted 'value' baskets, and C-grade to processing partners.
Guarantee the grade at delivery with instant credit if it fails.
solution.model: Supply produce to quick-commerce platforms at a grading premium; run own value baskets.
solution.gtm: Sell into two quick-commerce dark stores as a pilot, then expand city by city.
solution.moat: Grading standards and cold-chain handling data that reduce wastage.

market.tam: ₹80,000 Cr fresh produce retail; grading a quality wedge

problems.verdict: Quick commerce optimised speed; the next battle is consistency.

problems.title: How do people moving struggle to dispose old furniture?
problems.description: Families relocating to new apartments or cities cannot easily sell, donate, or responsibly dispose of old sofas, beds, wardrobes, and appliances because second-hand furniture markets are unorganized, online platforms attract only lowball offers, and municipalities don't provide convenient bulk furniture recycling or pickup services.
problems.who: Families relocating who cannot sell a sofa and will not dump it on the street.
problems.pitch: Doorstep furniture pickup with instant value estimates, resale, donation and certified recycling in one flow.

how: Quote from photos and dimensions, then pick up within 48 hours with a two-person crew.
Route usable items to resale or donation partners and the rest to certified recycling, with a diversion certificate.
Pay the customer instantly for resale-grade items and charge a flat fee for disposal-only jobs.
solution.model: Resale margin, disposal fees, and B2B office clearance contracts.
solution.price: ₹499–₹1,499 disposal; instant buy for 10–25% of resale value.
solution.gtm: Moving companies, real-estate agents and apartment handover groups.
solution.moat: Pickup density and resale/donation channel partnerships.

problems.verdict: The value is in the pickup, not the listing.

problems.title: Why can't doctors access patient medical histories across hospitals?
problems.description: Doctors treating patients in emergencies or follow-up visits across different hospitals cannot access consolidated medical histories, previous prescriptions, drug allergy information, or ongoing medication regimens because health records remain fragmented across individual hospitals with no interoperable national health database system.
problems.who: Patients repeating tests because the new hospital cannot see the old file.
problems.pitch: A patient-owned record that pulls history from every hospital and shares it with a doctor through a consent link.

how: Integrate with ABDM/ABHA and hospital HMIS systems to pull prescriptions, labs and discharge summaries into one timeline.
Let the patient grant time-limited, revocable access to a specific doctor via a QR or link.
Add an offline PDF pack for hospitals that are not yet digital.
solution.model: Free consumer vault; hospital integration fees; insurer partnerships.
solution.gtm: ABDM sandbox partners, hospital chains and insurance claim teams.
solution.moat: Hospital integrations and patient consent graph.

problems.verdict: The patient should own the record, not the hospital that happened to be visited.

problems.title: Why can’t heirs access bank accounts easily after a death?
problems.description: Families face financial paralysis because succession processes remain paperwork-heavy and fragmented, making it difficult to securely transfer access to assets after a person’s death.
problems.who: Families locked out of a deceased relative's accounts and policies.
problems.pitch: A guided succession workflow that inventories accounts, audits nominations and coordinates with banks after a death.

how: Build a secure asset inventory the account holder can maintain, including nominations and document locations.
On a claim, generate a bank-specific document pack and track each institution's process and SLA.
Partner with probate lawyers and offer a paid done-for-you service for complex estates.
mvp: Document pack generator for five banks
solution.model: Annual vault subscription plus a success fee on claims.
solution.gtm: Estate lawyers, senior-citizen associations and private bankers.
solution.moat: Bank process maps and case outcomes.

market.tam: ₹1,200 Cr estate settlement services, largely informal

problems.verdict: Grief is not a workflow — but the paperwork can be.

problems.title: Why can’t rural residents receive doorstep deliveries despite ordering products online?
problems.description: Residents of small villages and remote rural areas cannot access the full benefits of online shopping because delivery partners refuse to service locations without proper addresses or road access, forcing villagers to travel 10-20 kilometers to district headquarters to collect packages from centralized hubs.
problems.who: Rural shoppers forced to travel 10–20 km to a district hub for every parcel.
problems.pitch: Village-level delivery through a trusted local shop, with address normalisation and pooled last-mile routes.

how: Onboard kirana shops as pickup points and equip them with a parcel app and OTP handover.
Normalise rural addresses using landmarks, phone numbers and geo-pins at the point of order.
Pool parcels from multiple couriers into one daily route per cluster.
solution.model: Per-parcel last-mile fee from couriers/marketplaces plus a commission on assisted orders.
solution.gtm: Partner with one marketplace and two regional couriers; start in one district with dense village clusters.
solution.moat: Village-level partner network and address data.

market.tam: ₹8,000 Cr rural last-mile, growing with e-commerce penetration

problems.verdict: The last mile in rural India is a person, not a route.

problems.title: Why can’t working professionals return online purchases outside of business hours?
problems.description: Employees working 9-to-6 jobs who need to return online purchases cannot coordinate delivery-partner pickup schedules that only operate during business hours when they are away from home, and they lack access to convenient 24/7 smart locker systems where they can drop off returns independently.
problems.who: 9-to-6 professionals who cannot wait at home for a pickup slot.
problems.pitch: A 24/7 locker network for e-commerce returns, with drop-off in two minutes at the corner store.

how: Install smart lockers in kirana stores and society gates, with barcode-based drop-off and size-based compartments.
Integrate with marketplaces to generate a return label and auto-notify the courier for bulk pickup.
Compensate the host store per parcel and track chain of custody to the warehouse.
solution.model: Per-parcel handling fee from marketplaces plus locker advertising.
solution.gtm: Sign two marketplaces for reverse-logistics volume, then expand the locker network.
solution.moat: Locker density and host-store relationships.

market.tam: ₹1.2 lakh Cr e-commerce; returns 8–12% of GMV

problems.verdict: Returns are the unglamorous half of e-commerce, and still unbuilt.

problems.title: How do users reconcile bank statement transactions monthly?
problems.description: Individuals reviewing monthly bank statements cannot remember what each transaction was for after 15-30 days. UPI transactions show cryptic merchant IDs. Small payments of ₹50-200 are unidentifiable. Tagging or categorizing transactions post-facto is tedious. No automatic transaction description and categorization exists, making expense tracking and budget analysis nearly impossible without extensive manual work.
problems.who: Individuals staring at ₹50 debits coded as 'UPI/1234567890'.
problems.pitch: Every bank and UPI transaction auto-labelled with a real merchant name, a note and a category you can trust.

how: Resolve merchant IDs to brands using a payments-merchant graph, and let users confirm or correct the label once.
Auto-suggest notes from calendar, email receipts and prior behaviour, then categorise with a personal rules engine.
Generate a month-end reconciliation view that flags duplicates, subscriptions and unusual charges.
solution.model: Freemium consumer app; white-label reconciliation for accountants.
solution.price: Free for one account; ₹99/month for unlimited.
solution.gtm: Personal-finance creators and CA firms serving salaried clients.
solution.moat: The merchant-ID graph, which improves with every correction.

problems.verdict: The cryptic merchant ID is the root of every budgeting failure.

problems.title: Why can't EV drivers see real-time charger availability?
problems.description: Electric vehicle drivers waste time and battery charge navigating to public charging stations listed on apps only to discover they are non-functional, under maintenance, or occupied, and they need real-time verification systems that confirm charger availability, functionality status, and queuing times before departure.
problems.who: EV owners burned by apps listing chargers that are broken or occupied.
problems.pitch: Verified real-time charger status — working, occupied, queue length — before an EV driver commits to the detour.

how: Pull status from charger operators via OCPP/API where available, and fill gaps with a driver check-in button and a 15-minute freshness rule.
Show queue estimates, connector type compatibility and a one-tap reservation where operators allow it.
Sell the verified status feed to map apps, fleets and OEM navigation systems.
solution.model: Operator subscriptions, fleet SaaS and data licensing.
solution.gtm: Charger operators who want utilisation, OEM apps and fleet operators.
solution.moat: Status coverage and a reliability score per charger.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr EV charging software and data

problems.verdict: The charging network's real problem is trust in the map.

problems.title: Why do rural patients waste time traveling for diagnostic tests?
problems.description: Patients in small towns and villages requiring basic blood tests, X-rays, or ultrasounds must travel 30-50 kilometers to reach diagnostic laboratories in larger cities, wasting entire days in transit and delaying treatment decisions because mobile diagnostic vans or local sample collection services are unavailable in rural areas.
problems.who: Rural patients travelling 30–50 km for a basic blood test.
problems.pitch: Doorstep sample collection in villages, with a daily pickup route to a certified lab and reports back on WhatsApp.

how: Train local phlebotomists and equip them with cold-chain sample boxes and a route app.
Tie up with accredited labs for testing and return reports in the patient's language on WhatsApp.
Add a mobile X-ray/ultrasound van on a weekly circuit for imaging tests.
solution.model: Per-test margin shared with the lab; government and insurer contracts.
solution.gtm: Primary health centres, ASHA networks and district lab partners.
solution.moat: Village-level collection density and cold-chain reliability.

market.tam: ₹20,000 Cr diagnostics; rural access a large gap

problems.verdict: Bring the lab to the sample, not the patient to the lab.

problems.title: Why is distinguishing sprains from fractures impossible without costly hospital visits?
problems.description: A ₹1,500 hospital visit, a four-hour wait and an X-ray read by whoever is on duty. Imaging is centralised and expensive. Triage is guesswork, so everyone defaults to the emergency room.
problems.who: People with ankle, wrist or knee injuries in tier-1 and tier-2 cities, especially at night or after sport.
problems.pitch: A ₹399 scan-and-triage service that tells you whether it is a sprain or a fracture, without the hospital queue.

how: Put portable X-ray or ultrasound in partner pharmacies and micro-clinics, with a radiographer on a fixed protocol.
Run AI-assisted fracture triage, then have a radiologist sign off before the report reaches the patient.
Return a 30-minute report with a clear next step: home care, immobilisation kit or orthopaedic referral.
solution.model: Per-scan fee, insurer and employer contracts, referral share.
solution.price: ₹399–699 per scan, with a ₹199 tele-review add-on.
solution.gtm: Pharmacy chains, sports academies and corporate health camps. Night-time availability is the wedge.
solution.moat: A distributed imaging network and an annotated triage dataset. Both compound with volume.

market.tam: ₹10,000 Cr+ diagnostic imaging market, with MSK injuries as a high-frequency entry point

problems.verdict: The hardest part of an injury is not the treatment, it is finding out how serious it is. Charge for the answer.

problems.title: Why can’t citizens verify whether segregated waste is actually recycled?
problems.description: Citizens diligently segregating wet and dry waste have no visibility into whether municipal collectors actually maintain segregation or mix everything. This undermines individual efforts. No verification system shows waste actually reaches recycling facilities versus landfills.
problems.who: Citizens who segregate diligently and suspect it all gets mixed in the truck.
problems.pitch: Track a household's segregated waste from bin to recycler, with weight and photo proof at every handoff.

how: Tag household bins with a QR and scan at collection, recording weight and a photo of the segregated bag.
Scan again at the transfer station and the recycling facility, and reconcile the chain to flag mixing.
Show residents a monthly diversion certificate and reward consistent segregation with municipal benefits.
solution.model: Municipal contracts, recycler fees and CSR sponsorship.
solution.gtm: Municipal solid-waste departments and resident welfare associations.
solution.moat: Verified diversion data and municipal relationships.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr waste management software and services

problems.verdict: Segregation only survives if someone can prove what happened next.

problems.title: Why can't first-time used car buyers verify car histories, conditions and future maintenance costs?
problems.description: A dealer's 12-point 'inspection', WhatsApp photos and a mechanic's gut feel. Service records stay with the workshop that did the work. Vehicle data is split across insurers, workshops, RTOs and dealers. Nobody in the transaction is rewarded for revealing the car's real condition.
problems.who: First-time buyers spending ₹3–12 lakh on a used car, often without a mechanic in the family.
problems.pitch: A verified history and condition dossier for first-time used-car buyers, built from the car's own data.

how: Pull registration, insurance and service history against the VIN, then run a 90-minute physical inspection with an OBD-II scan, paint-depth gauge and underbody photos.
Generate a condition report with a fair-price band and a 12-month maintenance forecast, not just a pass/fail checklist.
Back every dossier with a dispute window and a partner warranty, so the report carries financial weight.
mvp: Inspector app with a fixed 60-point protocol
Report web link with photo evidence
Two-city inspector network and 20 dealer supply partners
solution.model: Per-inspection fee, dealer subscriptions, commission on warranty and insurance attach.
solution.gtm: Sell through used-car marketplaces, car-loan agents and independent dealers. Rank for 'used car inspection + city' searches.
solution.moat: Longitudinal vehicle data, an inspector network and warranty partnerships. Each report makes the next valuation sharper.

market.tam: ₹40,000 Cr+ organised used-car market where inspection is the trust bottleneck

problems.verdict: Trust is the tax on India's used-car market. Whoever removes it owns the transaction.

problems.title: Why can’t manufacturers rely on guaranteed, accountable pickup logistics for outbound deliveries?
problems.description: Small-scale manufacturers frequently miss critical delivery deadlines and lose customer orders when local logistics providers and transport vendors fail to arrive for scheduled pick-ups, leaving products stranded at factories with no reliable alternative transportation networks to fall back on.
problems.who: D2C brands and manufacturers shipping outbound from two or three warehouses.
problems.pitch: SLA-backed first-mile pickup with proof, penalties and payout on delivery.

how: Book pickup slots with vetted fleets and attach a penalty-backed SLA to every slot.
Capture photo, weight and condition proof at pickup, then release payment only after confirmed delivery.
Run an exception desk for damages and delays, with insurance attached to high-value loads.
mvp: Two anchor clients on monthly SLA
solution.model: Per-pickup fee plus an SLA subscription, insurance commission.
solution.gtm: D2C clusters in NCR and Bengaluru, plus 3PL partnerships that lack first-mile reliability.
solution.moat: Reliability data and driver density. Operations discipline is the barrier.

risks: Capex if the fleet is owned

market.tam: ₹20,000 Cr+ first-mile logistics spend, growing with D2C

problems.verdict: Brands sell a delivery promise. First-mile is where that promise quietly breaks.

problems.title: Why do fashion products look different in reality?
problems.description: Online fashion shoppers frequently receive garments that look dramatically different in person compared to professional product photographs, discovering mismatched colors, unexpected fabric quality, and poor fits because listings lack authentic user-generated video reviews showing items on real people with varied body types.
problems.who: Online fashion buyers burned by photos that hide fit, fabric and colour.
problems.pitch: Short video reviews from shoppers with the same body measurements, embedded on the product page.

how: Incentivise buyers to record a 15-second review with height, size worn and a fit rating.
Match reviews to the shopper's measurements and show only relevant clips on the product page.
Sell the widget to brands with a return-rate dashboard.
mvp: Review capture flow and measurement profile
solution.model: Brand SaaS plus a per-video bounty.
solution.gtm: Start with 20 D2C apparel brands; use return-rate reduction as the sales pitch.
solution.moat: A measurement-tagged review library that compounds.

market.tam: ₹60,000 Cr online fashion; returns are a ₹6,000 Cr cost pool

problems.verdict: Fit content is the cheapest return-reduction technology available.

problems.title: Why is caring for aging parents for sole earners across cities still fragmented & stressful?
problems.description: WhatsApp groups, a local attendant, and emergency calls that arrive after the fall, not before. Care is informal and unverified. Families have no single record of medicines, appointments and incidents, so every sibling becomes a project manager.
problems.who: Sole earners in metros with parents in another city, plus NRI siblings coordinating from abroad.
problems.pitch: One accountable layer for aging parents: care, records and a family dashboard across cities.

how: Build a vetted caregiver and attendant network with background checks, replacement SLAs and trained geriatric aides.
Run a shared care plan: medication log, appointments, vitals from a home BP/SpO2 kit, and incident notes visible to every sibling.
Add an escalation desk with partner hospitals and a monthly family review call led by a care manager.
solution.model: Monthly care subscription, hourly visits, commission on diagnostics and pharmacy.
solution.gtm: Geriatric clinics, apartment communities and NRI associations. Care managers close the sale, not ads.
solution.moat: Trust operations and longitudinal family records. Reliability is the product.

market.tam: India's 14 crore+ senior population, with a fast-growing paid-care segment

problems.verdict: The buyer is guilty, far away and has money. That is the most reliable demand signal in healthcare.

problems.title: Why are diagnostic services not designed for women’s privacy and mobility needs?
problems.description: Female patients, particularly married women in conservative areas, postpone essential diagnostic tests because medical facilities and transportation options lack adequate privacy, female-friendly infrastructure, or same-gender accompaniment services that would allow them to visit clinics independently without male family escorts.
problems.who: Women in conservative areas postponing tests because they cannot travel alone or face male staff.
problems.pitch: Women-only diagnostic visits with female phlebotomists, home collection and privacy-first transport.

how: Build an all-women collection and sonography assistant team, with home visits and a female attendant.
Offer private, appointment-only slots and a discreet report delivery channel.
Partner with local transport providers vetted for women's safety for clinic visits that need equipment.
solution.model: Per-test margin plus a subscription for antenatal and chronic panels.
solution.gtm: Women's self-help groups, gynaecologists and district health programmes.
solution.moat: A trusted all-women network in conservative geographies.

problems.verdict: Privacy is a clinical requirement, not a courtesy.

problems.title: Why can't consumers track sugar content in packaged snacks?
problems.description: Health-conscious consumers trying to limit sugar intake cannot accurately track consumption from packaged Indian snacks, biscuits, and beverages. Nutrition labels use grams rather than teaspoons, making it difficult to understand actual sugar quantities. Hidden sugars in savory products surprise consumers. No app aggregates and simplifies sugar content data for commonly consumed Indian packaged foods based on barcode scanning.
problems.who: Health-conscious shoppers confused by grams on the back of a biscuit pack.
problems.pitch: Scan any Indian packaged snack and see its sugar in teaspoons, plus hidden sugars in savoury products.

how: Build a barcode database of Indian packaged foods with sugar, additives and serving sizes, normalised to teaspoons.
Flag hidden sugars in savoury categories and compare products within the same aisle.
Add a daily sugar budget and a family profile with weekly intake summaries.
solution.model: Freemium app; brand-sponsored healthier alternatives; nutritionist partnerships.
solution.gtm: Health influencers, diabetes clinics, and school nutrition programmes.
solution.moat: A normalised Indian food-composition database.

problems.verdict: Grams do not change behaviour; teaspoons might.

problems.title: Why do factory owners wait days for industrial repair technicians?
problems.description: When specialized machinery breaks down in small manufacturing units, owners face multi-day production halts because there is no on-demand network or marketplace connecting them with qualified industrial technicians who can diagnose and repair niche equipment quickly.
problems.who: Factory owners and plant managers with a production line down.
problems.pitch: Industrial repair in hours, with vetted technicians and remote diagnostics first.

how: Verify technicians by machine type and skill, with a live availability calendar across industrial clusters.
Run remote video triage before dispatch, so the right technician and part arrive together.
Price on an SLA and share a downtime calculator that makes the cost of waiting explicit.
mvp: Spare-part partners for top 20 failure modes
solution.model: Commission on jobs, annual maintenance contracts, parts margin.
solution.gtm: Industrial associations, machine OEMs and plant WhatsApp groups.
solution.moat: Technician density and repair history by machine model. The data makes dispatch smarter.

market.tam: ₹25,000 Cr+ industrial maintenance and repair spend

problems.verdict: A day of downtime can cost more than a year of the repair contract. Price the urgency, not the hour.

problems.title: Why don’t smart water systems detect underground leaks automatically?
problems.description: Municipal water authorities waste 40% of water supply through underground pipeline leaks that go undetected for months. Citizens face shortages while water is lost. No acoustic leak detection or citizen reporting systems exist for identifying underground water wastage.
problems.who: Municipal water boards losing 40% of supply; residents facing dry taps.
problems.pitch: Acoustic sensors on the water network plus citizen reports that pinpoint a leak before it drains a colony's supply.

how: Clamp acoustic loggers onto mains at intervals and detect leak signatures from vibration patterns.
Correlate with citizen reports and pressure data to localise the leak to a 50-metre segment.
Dispatch a repair crew and measure water recovered per fix to prove the ROI.
solution.model: Municipal subscription plus a share of water saved.
solution.gtm: Water utilities in leak-prone cities and smart-city missions.
solution.moat: Leak-signature data by pipe material and age.

problems.verdict: The water is already being lost; the sensor just makes it visible.

problems.title: Why hasn’t tutoring shifted from answer-giving to skill-building learning?
problems.description: Parents hiring private tutors to help with challenging math and science subjects discover their children remain weak in fundamentals because tutors simply solve homework problems on students' behalf rather than explaining underlying concepts, principles, and problem-solving approaches that build genuine understanding.
problems.who: Parents paying for tutors while their child still cannot solve unseen problems.
problems.pitch: Tutoring that is contractually not allowed to give answers — diagnostic, Socratic sessions with a mastery score after every topic.

how: Diagnose the specific gap with a short adaptive test, then run sessions where the tutor may only ask questions and set sub-steps.
End each topic with an unseen problem set; a pass unlocks the next topic and triggers a parent report.
Train tutors on the protocol and audit session recordings for answer-giving.
mvp: Parent progress report and mastery map
solution.model: Per-session fee with a monthly learning report; school after-hours contracts.
solution.gtm: Parent communities and school PTAs; lead with the diagnostic, not the tutor.
solution.moat: A mastery map per student and a trained tutor protocol.

problems.verdict: Sell the outcome, not the hour.

problems.title: How can online platforms enable price negotiation and bulk discounts?
problems.description: Online shoppers accustomed to traditional retail's bargaining culture feel they overpay on e-commerce platforms because there is no mechanism allowing them to negotiate prices, request bulk discounts for multiple purchases, or propose alternate pricing for slightly older inventory or products nearing expiration.
problems.who: Shoppers who miss bargaining; D2C brands sitting on slow-moving or near-expiry stock.
problems.pitch: An offer-and-counter layer for online retail, with volume tiers and clearance pricing built in.

how: Give brands a rules engine to set floor prices, volume tiers and expiry-based discounts.
Let shoppers make an offer or start a group buy; the engine auto-accepts, counters or expires.
Settle the order on the brand's existing checkout so no new payment rail is needed.
solution.model: Success fee on incremental sales plus a SaaS tier for brands.
solution.gtm: Land 30 D2C brands with excess inventory; consumer launch through group-buy deals.
solution.moat: Pricing-response data across brands and categories.

market.tam: ₹1.5 lakh Cr online retail; negotiation a wedge into D2C

problems.verdict: India never stopped bargaining — online retail just forgot how.

problems.title: Why is reward visibility missing across UPI and wallet ecosystems?
problems.description: Consumers using multiple payment apps (Paytm, PhonePe, Google Pay, Amazon Pay) cannot track total cashback earned, pending amounts, and expiring offers across platforms. Each app has different reward structures and expiry timelines. Users miss out on claiming earned cashback or using expiring rewards. No unified dashboard shows total earnings and pending actions across all payment apps.
problems.who: Users juggling PhonePe, Paytm, GPay and Amazon Pay rewards without a total.
problems.pitch: One dashboard for cashback earned, pending and expiring across every payment app and wallet.

how: Ingest reward notifications from SMS, email and account linking into a single ledger.
Show earned, pending and expiring amounts by app, with a claim checklist for each.
Alert before expiry and recommend the best redemption path per platform.
solution.model: Affiliate redemptions and a premium tier.
solution.gtm: Frugal-living communities and UPI-heavy user segments.
solution.moat: Cross-platform reward data and expiry patterns.

problems.verdict: Rewards expire quietly; a ledger makes them loud.
