problems.title: How can buyers verify alcohol authenticity before purchase?
problems.description: Alcohol consumers fear purchasing counterfeit or adulterated liquor from retail shops, especially for premium brands. News reports of methanol poisoning and fake alcohol deaths create anxiety. Bottles lack tamper-evident seals or authentication mechanisms. Buyers in tier 2/3 cities particularly worry about product authenticity. No scan-based verification system allows customers to confirm genuine alcohol at point of purchase before opening bottles.
problems.who: Premium spirits buyers in tier-2/3 cities worried about counterfeit and adulterated bottles.
problems.pitch: A tamper-evident cap and scan-to-verify code that proves a bottle is genuine before it is opened.

how: Co-design a tamper-evident cap seal with a unique QR that breaks on opening, and issue codes to brands at bottling.
Let buyers scan in-app to see brand, batch, bottling date and whether the code has already been used.
Work with excise-compliant retailers and flag suspicious duplicate scans to the brand.
mvp: Cap seal prototype and code registry
solution.model: Per-seal fee from brands, plus retailer verification subscriptions.
solution.gtm: Pilot with one premium brand in one state; use an authenticity guarantee as the retail hook.
solution.moat: Brand seal adoption and a scan ledger that detects diversion.

market.tam: ₹45,000 Cr spirits retail; counterfeit fear is widespread

problems.verdict: Authentication has to happen before the first pour.

problems.title: Why do regional logistics lack real-time tracking and reliable delivery ETAs?
problems.description: Businesses shipping via local transport companies or smaller couriers have zero real-time tracking visibility. Customers call repeatedly for delivery updates. ETA predictions are unreliable. No unified tracking API exists for regional logistics providers, forcing businesses to manually coordinate delivery communications.
problems.who: SMEs shipping through local transport companies that still run on phone calls.
problems.pitch: A tracking and ETA layer that sits on top of regional couriers, using a driver app and WhatsApp scans instead of API integrations.

how: Give each regional courier a driver app or WhatsApp flow to scan LR numbers at pickup, transit and delivery.
Normalise the events into one tracking API and a customer-facing tracking page with a predicted ETA.
Sell the tracking page to shippers and the ops dashboard to couriers.
mvp: ETA model trained on lane history
solution.model: SaaS per shipper plus a per-scan fee from couriers.
solution.gtm: Regional transport associations and SME exporter clusters.
solution.moat: Lane-level event data and courier network coverage.

problems.verdict: You do not need every courier's API — you need the driver's phone.

problems.title: Why is finding specialist doctors in smaller cities hard?
problems.description: Patients in tier 2 and tier 3 cities needing consultations with neurologists, cardiologists, oncologists, or other super-specialists face appointment wait times of 3-4 weeks or must travel to metro cities because there are too few specialists serving large populations and no telemedicine platforms connecting them efficiently.
problems.who: Tier-2/3 patients waiting three weeks or travelling to a metro for a cardiologist.
problems.pitch: Tele-specialist appointments within 48 hours, supported by a local clinic room and a trained nurse for the examination.

how: Recruit super-specialists for scheduled tele-slots and partner with local clinics that provide an exam room and nurse.
Ship or use local diagnostic devices — ECG, stethoscope, ultrasound probe — so the consult is not just a video call.
Close the loop with a local prescription, lab order and follow-up scheduled in the same flow.
solution.model: Consultation fee share plus clinic and lab referral revenue.
solution.gtm: Local clinics, pharmacy chains and district hospital referral desks.
solution.moat: Specialist supply and clinic coverage outside metros.

problems.verdict: Telemedicine fails without a room, a nurse and a device.

problems.title: How can regional menus be made more accessible for interstate travellers?
problems.description: Travelers from different regions struggle to understand restaurant menus written exclusively in regional scripts and they need instant visual AI translation apps that can scan and convert menu images into their preferred language with food descriptions.
problems.who: Interstate travellers staring at a menu in a script they cannot read.
problems.pitch: Scan any regional menu and get it in your language, with dish explanations, allergens and a pronunciation guide.

how: Build OCR for Indian scripts plus a dish knowledge base with ingredients, spice level and allergens.
Translate into the traveller's language and add audio pronunciation and a 'what to order' shortlist.
Let restaurants upload a structured menu so travellers see it before arriving.
mvp: OCR and translation for four scripts
solution.model: Freemium app, restaurant listings and travel affiliate revenue.
solution.price: Free; ₹99/month for offline packs and allergy filters.
solution.gtm: Travel creators, tourism boards and restaurant associations.
solution.moat: Dish-level data and script OCR accuracy.

problems.verdict: The menu is the last un-translated interface in travel.

problems.title: Why do hidden shipping fees inflate affordable product prices?
problems.description: Budget-conscious shoppers attracted to affordably-priced products on e-commerce platforms experience frustration at checkout when previously hidden or unclear shipping fees, handling charges, and platform fees suddenly inflate the total cost by 30-50%, making the purchase no longer economically viable.
problems.who: Budget shoppers who abandon checkout when a ₹499 item becomes ₹749.
problems.pitch: The landed price before you commit — shipping, handling and platform fees surfaced at product-list level.

how: Compute landed cost from pincode, weight, seller and payment method, then display it on the listing page.
Ship as a browser extension and a price-comparison site that ranks by total cost, not sticker price.
Track fee changes over time and alert users when a seller quietly raises shipping.
solution.model: Affiliate commissions, promoted honest sellers, and a data API for consumer advocates.
solution.price: Free to consumers; affiliate revenue per redirected purchase.
solution.gtm: Launch on Product Hunt and frugal-living communities; publish a 'hidden fee index' for press.
solution.moat: Fee-data history and comparison SEO.

market.tam: ₹1.5 lakh Cr online retail; fee transparency a media and affiliate play

problems.verdict: The sticker price is a lie; being the honest number is a brand.

problems.title: Why do resumes fail ATS filters despite candidates being qualified for roles?
problems.description: Fresh graduates and career switchers applying to dozens of entry-level positions receive no response or interview callbacks because corporate ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems) automatically filter out resumes lacking specific keywords, employer brand names, or exact experience criteria, and candidates lack guidance on optimizing applications for AI screening.
problems.who: Fresh graduates and career switchers sending 50 applications into a void.
problems.pitch: An ATS-readiness tool that rewrites for the specific job and proves the skills with a portfolio, not just keywords.

how: Parse the job description and the resume, then show exactly which requirements are missing or phrased badly for ATS.
Generate role-specific bullet variants that stay truthful, with a diff the candidate approves.
Attach a verified skills portfolio and run a mock screening interview for the same role.
solution.model: Freemium with a paid application pack; university career-cell licences.
solution.price: ₹299 per application pack; ₹999 for five roles; ₹50,000/year college licence.
solution.gtm: Campus placement cells, LinkedIn content, and a free ATS score as the hook.
solution.moat: Application-outcome data tied to resume changes.

problems.verdict: Keywords get you parsed; evidence gets you hired.

problems.title: Why do small online orders arrive in oversized wasteful packaging?
problems.description: Environmentally conscious consumers ordering single items or small products online feel frustrated when deliveries arrive in oversized boxes filled with excessive bubble wrap, plastic padding, and unnecessary packaging materials, and they want sustainable "right-sized" or reusable eco-friendly bag delivery options instead.
problems.who: E-commerce warehouses over-boxing small orders; eco-conscious shoppers buried in plastic.
problems.pitch: Right-sized, reusable packaging for e-commerce — engineered per order, not picked from three box sizes.

how: Feed order dimensions into a cartonisation algorithm that selects or cuts the smallest viable mailer.
Offer a reusable mailer with a ₹50 deposit that is collected on the next delivery.
Report packaging waste and cost saved per 1,000 orders to the brand.
solution.model: Packaging supply margin plus a per-order optimisation fee.
solution.price: ₹6–₹18 per order; reusable mailer ₹35 with ₹50 deposit.
solution.gtm: Target D2C brands with sustainability commitments and 5,000+ monthly orders.
solution.moat: Order-profile data and a deposit-return network.

market.tam: ₹60,000 Cr e-commerce logistics; packaging a ₹4,000 Cr slice

problems.verdict: Packaging is a cost line and a brand signal at the same time.

problems.title: Why hasn’t late-night women’s mobility been solved with tech-enabled safety systems?
problems.description: Women working night shifts, traveling after social events, or returning home late avoid auto-rickshaws and cabs due to safety concerns and instead need dedicated women-only driver networks with verified female chauffeurs, panic buttons, live journey tracking, and emergency response systems for secure nighttime transportation.
problems.who: Women working night shifts or returning late who do not trust a random cab.
problems.pitch: A women-only driver network for late nights, with live tracking, a panic button and a response team that actually calls back.

how: Recruit and verify women drivers with background checks, a safety training module and an in-ride SOS device.
Share live trip details with two emergency contacts and run a 24/7 response desk with a 60-second callback SLA.
Restrict late-night trips to verified riders and drivers, and publish safety response times.
solution.model: Ride commission plus a corporate night-shift transport contract.
solution.price: ₹40–₹70 per late-night trip; corporate plans per seat.
solution.gtm: BPO and hospital night-shift employers, women's employee resource groups, and campus networks.
solution.moat: A verified women driver network and measured response times.

problems.verdict: Safety is not a feature toggle; it is a response team.

problems.title: Why isn’t subscription pause logic built into auto-debit infrastructure?
problems.description: Users traveling abroad, facing temporary financial constraints, or wanting to skip a month of gym/subscription services cannot pause auto-debit mandates temporarily. The only option is permanent cancellation followed by re-enrollment with new KYC and setup. This forces users to continue paying for unused services for 1-3 months. No temporary freeze option exists for UPI autopay, e-mandates, or standing instructions.
problems.who: Subscribers travelling or between jobs who keep paying for unused gym, OTT and SaaS plans.
problems.pitch: A one-tap pause for UPI autopay and card mandates — freeze for a month or three instead of cancelling and redoing KYC.

how: Build a consumer app that lists active mandates via the bank/UPI mandate APIs and offers a pause window.
Work with merchants to honour pause windows through a standard SDK and a pause-aware billing schedule.
Resume automatically on the chosen date, with a reminder 48 hours before the next debit.
solution.model: Small fee per paused mandate plus merchant SaaS for churn reduction.
solution.gtm: Gym and OTT partnerships; consumer launch around travel and job-change seasons.
solution.moat: Merchant integrations and mandate-level retention data.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr subscription billing; pause a retention wedge

problems.verdict: Cancellation is a churn event; pause is a retention product.

problems.title: Why can't businesses verify new suppliers before purchasing?
problems.description: Small businesses looking to source raw materials from unfamiliar suppliers face substantial risks of receiving substandard goods, inconsistent quality, or outright fraud because there is no centralized verification system or B2B trust rating infrastructure to validate vendor credentials and track performance before committing to purchases.
problems.who: Procurement teams at mid-market manufacturers and D2C brands onboarding new suppliers.
problems.pitch: A trust score for new suppliers, built from registries, audits and live delivery data.

how: Pull GST, ROC, litigation and credit signals into one report with a plain-language risk score.
Add a quality audit from a vetted inspector and verified references from actual buyers.
Monitor the supplier continuously and alert the buyer when filings, ownership or delivery performance change.
solution.model: Per-report fee, annual monitoring subscription, audit fees.
solution.gtm: Procurement consultants, industry bodies and B2B marketplaces that need a trust layer.
solution.moat: Supplier graph and audit history. Every report improves the next one.

market.tam: ₹5 lakh Cr+ in annual B2B procurement, with supplier onboarding as the entry point

problems.verdict: Buyers already pay for due diligence with time and bad debt. Sell it as a report they can defend.

problems.title: Why can’t citizens quickly find the right animal rescue help during emergencies?
problems.description: Compassionate citizens encountering injured, sick, or trapped stray animals feel helpless because they don't know which NGO, veterinary service, or municipal department to contact for rescue assistance, and they need a unified emergency animal rescue app aggregating contact information for nearest rescue organizations based on GPS location.
problems.who: Good samaritans who spot an injured animal and do not know whom to call.
problems.pitch: One GPS-aware number for injured strays — it finds the nearest rescue NGO, vet or municipal van and dispatches the right one.

how: Aggregate verified rescuers, NGOs, vets and municipal animal vans by service area and capability.
Triage the case with three questions and dispatch to the nearest capable responder, with a live status to the caller.
Log outcomes and response times, and route donations to the rescues that actually show up.
mvp: Caller web app with photo upload
solution.model: Grants and donations, plus vet/ambulance referral fees; municipal contracts.
solution.gtm: Animal welfare communities, municipal animal welfare boards, and vet clinics.
solution.moat: Responder network coverage and outcome data.

market.tam: ₹800 Cr animal welfare services, largely donation-funded

problems.verdict: A coordination layer can save lives without owning a single ambulance.

problems.title: Why do branded drugs dominate prescriptions despite equivalent, cheaper generic alternatives?
problems.description: Doctors and patients continue prescribing expensive branded pharmaceuticals over affordable generic equivalents containing the same active ingredients and dosages because of lingering suspicions about generic quality, manufacturing standards, bioavailability, and effectiveness despite regulatory equivalence certifications.
problems.who: Patients overpaying 3–10x for brands; doctors unsure about generic quality.
problems.pitch: Generic substitution made trustworthy: quality-test reports, bioavailability evidence and a doctor-facing switch tool.

how: Publish batch-level quality test results for generic manufacturers from accredited labs.
Give doctors a substitution tool that maps brand to salt, dose and therapeutic equivalence with evidence.
Offer patients a pharmacy switch with the same molecule at a lower price and a pharmacist review.
solution.model: Pharmacy margin, manufacturer verification fees and insurer partnerships.
solution.price: 10–15% of the price difference; free to doctors.
solution.gtm: Physician associations, insurer networks and corporate pharmacy programmes.
solution.moat: Independent quality data on generics.

market.tam: ₹2 lakh Cr pharma retail; substitution a large savings pool

problems.verdict: Generics do not need marketing; they need evidence.

problems.title: Why do freelancers ghost projects after partial payments without accountability systems?
problems.description: Businesses hiring ad-hoc freelancers through informal channels experience high churn rates when workers disappear mid-project after receiving partial payments, leaving companies with incomplete deliverables and no legal framework to recover damages or enforce completion.
problems.who: Freelancers and small agencies working with clients they have never met.
problems.pitch: Milestone escrow and dispute resolution for freelance projects, so nobody ghosts.

how: Create milestone contracts with funded escrow before work starts, so the money exists before the deliverable.
Release funds on approval, with a structured revision window instead of endless feedback.
Provide mediation and a small-claims arbitration panel, plus portable reputation across clients.
solution.model: Escrow fee, premium contracts, arbitration fees.
solution.price: 1.5–2.5% of escrowed value. ₹299 for a custom contract.
solution.gtm: Freelancer communities, agency networks and invoicing tools that already hold the relationship.
solution.moat: Dispute data and a portable trust graph. Regulation is a barrier and a moat.

market.tam: India's 1.5 crore+ freelance workforce and its unpaid-invoice problem

problems.verdict: Both sides of a freelance deal are afraid. A neutral referee can charge both of them.

problems.title: Why isn't there a women-first travel app for solo travellers?
problems.description: Solo women travelers and backpackers exploring unfamiliar cities face safety concerns about getting lost, experiencing harassment, or encountering emergencies far from home, and they need verified local guardian networks of background-checked residents they can contact immediately if they feel threatened or require urgent assistance.
problems.who: Solo women travellers who want local help without relying on strangers online.
problems.pitch: A women-first travel app with verified local guardians, safety maps and a one-tap SOS that reaches a real person nearby.

how: Recruit background-checked local guardians — residents, hostel owners, women-led businesses — with a verification interview.
Map safe areas, transport and verified stays, and let travellers request a guardian meet-up or a check-in call.
Run a 24/7 SOS line with location sharing and a local escalation partner.
solution.model: Membership, guardian commission and safety-certified stay listings.
solution.gtm: Solo-travel communities, women's travel creators and hostels.
solution.moat: A verified guardian network in each city.

problems.verdict: Safety at a destination is a supply network, not a panic button.

problems.title: Why don’t parents get real-time visibility when school buses run late?
problems.description: Parents experience extreme anxiety when their children's school buses run late without any communication explaining delays or confirming student safety, and they want GPS-tracked transportation with live interior cabin video feeds and automated arrival notifications to eliminate uncertainty about child whereabouts.
problems.who: Parents whose children ride a school bus with no communication when it runs late.
problems.pitch: Live school-bus tracking with boarding scans and delay alerts, so parents know where the child is without calling the school.

how: Install a GPS unit and a driver app that scans each child at boarding and drop-off.
Send parents a live map, a delay alert with a new ETA, and an arrival confirmation.
Give the school a dashboard for route exceptions and a transport audit log.
mvp: GPS unit and driver scan app
solution.model: Per-bus monthly SaaS paid by the school, passed into the fee.
solution.gtm: School transport heads and bus-operator associations; start with 50 buses in one city.
solution.moat: School contracts and route reliability data.

problems.verdict: A parent's anxiety is a notification away from relief.

problems.title: Why can't large families get wholesale grocery pricing online?
problems.description: Households with 6+ members or joint families that regularly purchase large quantities of groceries, cooking staples, and household essentials cannot obtain the same wholesale rates that restaurants and businesses receive because grocery apps only offer consumer retail pricing without volume-based discount tiers.
problems.who: Joint families and 6+ member households buying 20kg staples at retail rates.
problems.pitch: Wholesale grocery tiers for large households, with monthly staples delivered at distributor prices.

how: Build a monthly staples basket with volume tiers that unlock at 10kg, 25kg and 50kg.
Pool orders from nearby households to hit distributor minimums and pass the discount through.
Lock a monthly subscription with a delivery window and a price guarantee.
solution.model: Margin on staples plus a subscription fee.
solution.gtm: Apartment clusters and joint-family WhatsApp groups; start with atta, rice, oil and pulses.
solution.moat: Local pooling density and supplier terms.

market.tam: ₹40 lakh Cr grocery; bulk household a niche wedge

problems.verdict: Aggregate demand at the household level and the distributor margin comes back.

problems.title: Why don’t schools provide step-by-step, student-friendly kits for complex assignments?
problems.description: Elementary and middle school students assigned elaborate science fair projects, working models, or craft assignments rely heavily on parental intervention because schools assign overly complex tasks without providing age-appropriate guidance, pre-assembled DIY kits, or step-by-step student-friendly instruction materials.
problems.who: Parents of Class 3–8 students scrambling the night before a science fair.
problems.pitch: Age-appropriate project kits with materials, step cards and a safety check — so the assignment is the child's, not the parent's.

how: Map school project briefs to kit templates by grade and subject, with pre-cut materials and illustrated steps.
Design for independent completion in 45–90 minutes, with a 'parent hands off' instruction and a reflection sheet.
Ship a monthly kit subscription and a teacher pack for schools that assign projects.
solution.model: Subscription boxes plus school bulk orders.
solution.gtm: School partnerships at the start of term, parent groups, and Amazon/Flipkart listings.
solution.moat: Kit design library mapped to actual school curricula.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr school supplies and activity kits

problems.verdict: The customer is the parent, but the user must be the child.

problems.title: Why do businesses struggle finding reliable contract manufacturers for small batches?
problems.description: Startups and small brands needing 500-5,000 unit production runs cannot find contract manufacturers willing to accept small-batch orders. Most job-work units demand minimum orders of 10,000+ units or charge 40-50% premiums for small quantities. Quality consistency issues arise when manufacturers prioritize large clients. No B2B marketplace connects small brands with verified contract manufacturers offering flexible MOQs, transparent pricing, and quality guarantees for emerging businesses.
problems.who: D2C brands and hardware startups needing 500–5,000 units to test a market.
problems.pitch: Small-batch contract manufacturing, matched on capacity, quality and lead time.

how: Map factory capacity by machine, process and open slots, then expose only genuinely available small-batch windows.
Run a design-for-manufacturing check before quoting, so the buyer does not pay for an avoidable re-tool.
Hold a quality escrow: release payment after sample approval and a third-party inspection.
solution.model: Transaction fee, DFM services, inspection fees.
solution.price: 3–5% of order value. ₹5,000 per DFM review.
solution.gtm: D2C communities, accelerator cohorts and factory associations.
solution.moat: A factory-capacity graph with quality history. Supply is the hard side to build.

market.tam: ₹15,000 Cr+ small-batch contract manufacturing, driven by D2C

problems.verdict: Every D2C brand starts with a batch too small for a real factory. Be the bridge they never had.

problems.title: Why do courier companies lose or damage 5% of packages?
problems.description: E-commerce sellers and personal shippers face 3-5% package loss or damage rates during courier transit. Filing claims requires extensive documentation. Courier companies take 30-45 days for claim processing. Compensation is disputed or denied. Insurance options are expensive. No accountability mechanism ensures careful package handling.
problems.who: E-commerce sellers and individuals losing 3–5% of shipments to damage or loss.
problems.pitch: A chain-of-custody scan at every hop, with photo evidence and a claim decided in 48 hours instead of 45 days.

how: Give each parcel a QR that every handler scans, with a mandatory condition photo at pickup, hub and delivery.
Adjudicate claims from the scan trail and photos automatically, with a human review for high-value cases.
Offer per-shipment cover priced from the seller's actual damage history.
solution.model: Per-parcel fee plus insurance premium commission.
solution.price: ₹3–₹8 per parcel; cover from 0.4% of declared value.
solution.gtm: Start with D2C sellers doing 2,000+ shipments a month; prove claim-time reduction.
solution.moat: Claims and damage data by courier, route and packaging type.

market.tam: ₹1.2 lakh Cr e-commerce logistics; damage and loss a ₹4,000 Cr cost

problems.verdict: Proof at every hop turns an argument into a claim.

problems.title: How do users manage multiple payment app wallets?
problems.description: Users maintaining wallets in Paytm, PhonePe, Amazon Pay, and Mobikwik face fragmented balance management. Money sits idle across wallets. Transferring wallet balance to bank accounts incurs fees or isn't allowed. Checking balances across apps before payments is tedious. No wallet aggregator shows combined balance or allows inter-wallet transfers, forcing users to maintain ₹500-2,000 idle in each app.
problems.who: Users holding ₹500–2,000 idle in four wallets before every payment.
problems.pitch: See every wallet balance in one place and sweep idle money back to your bank in a tap.

how: Link wallet accounts through available APIs and notification parsing to show combined balance.
Offer a sweep to bank or a UPI top-up suggestion when a wallet is short, avoiding failed payments.
Recommend which wallet to pay from based on balance and offers at checkout.
solution.model: Affiliate top-up revenue and a small sweep fee.
solution.gtm: UPI-heavy users and wallet cashback communities.
solution.moat: Cross-wallet balance data and sweep rails.

problems.verdict: Idle float is a small pain with a large aggregate.

problems.title: Why can't elderly people find at-home beautician services?
problems.description: Senior citizens and people with mobility challenges face difficulty accessing basic beauty and grooming services like haircuts, manicures, or facials because very few beauty professionals offer home visit services, and those who do often charge prohibitively high premiums or have limited availability for residential appointments.
problems.who: Seniors and people with limited mobility who cannot travel to a salon; their adult children who book and pay.
problems.pitch: At-home beauty and grooming for seniors, delivered by therapists trained in mobility, skin fragility and dignity.

how: Train therapists on safe positioning, fragile-skin products, and a 45-minute low-movement service protocol.
Offer a fixed menu — haircut, manicure, facial, beard trim — with a caregiver present option and photo consent rules.
Build recurring monthly visits with the family, billed to the adult child living elsewhere.
solution.model: Per-visit fee plus a monthly subscription; B2B contracts with retirement communities.
solution.gtm: Tie-ups with elder-care agencies, retirement homes and geriatric clinics; the payer is the NRI or out-of-city child.
solution.moat: Trained therapist supply and trust with families, which compounds into recurring schedules.

market.tam: ₹2,500 Cr senior care services; beauty a small but high-intent slice

problems.verdict: The buyer and the user are different people — build for both.

problems.title: Why do makeup artists ignore diverse skin tones?
problems.description: Brides with diverse skin tones express frustration when makeup artists default to applying identical "fair and lovely" style makeup to all clients without customizing foundation shades, undertones, or techniques to enhance and celebrate each individual's natural complexion and ethnic beauty.
problems.who: Brides and event clients with medium-to-deep skin tones who have been 'fair-shaded' by artists trained on one default palette.
problems.pitch: A makeup-artist marketplace indexed by skin tone and undertone, so brides book artists who have actually worked on complexions like theirs.

how: Build artist portfolios that are searchable by shade range, undertone and skin type, with unedited before/after photos taken under the same lighting.
Certify artists on a diverse-shade curriculum developed with makeup educators, and publish the foundation/concealer lines each artist carries.
Let clients book a paid 20-minute shade consultation before the event, with the fee adjusted against the final booking.
mvp: Artist profile schema: shade range, undertone specialities, kit list, verified photos
Booking and consultation flow with deposits
solution.model: 15–20% booking commission, paid artist certification, and brand sampling fees for inclusive shade lines.
solution.price: ₹1,500–₹2,500 consultation; marketplace take rate 15% on ₹8,000–₹35,000 bookings.
solution.gtm: Launch in wedding-heavy cities through bridal communities and makeup-education institutes; publish a public 'shade-blind' salon index for PR.
solution.moat: A structured, verified portfolio of artists by shade range plus a certification standard that artists advertise.

risks: Supply of genuinely skilled artists is thin

market.tam: ₹12,000 Cr+ Indian beauty services, with bridal makeup the highest-ticket slice

problems.verdict: Inclusive beauty is a supply-verification problem before it is a branding problem.

problems.title: Why do STEM students face education loan anxiety from unclear costs in 2026?
problems.description: Glossy brochures, agent-led comparisons and a disbursement process that hides processing fees, insurance bundles and reset rates. Cost data is scattered across lenders and colleges, and the intermediary earns a commission on the loan, not on clarity.
problems.who: STEM aspirants and parents borrowing ₹8–40 lakh for private colleges.
problems.pitch: The true-cost layer for education loans: compare, simulate and track every rupee before and after admission.

how: Simulate the full cost of a course: tuition, hostel, living costs, moratorium interest and repayment under three salary scenarios.
Compare lenders on effective APR, foreclosure terms and disbursement conditions, with conflicts disclosed.
Track disbursement, fee demands and interest accrual in one document vault, then alert the borrower when refinancing beats the current loan.
solution.model: Disclosed lender lead fees, a paid planning tier, refinance commission.
solution.price: Free comparison. ₹499 for the planning vault. Refinance fee from the new lender.
solution.gtm: Admissions YouTube and Telegram communities, test-prep partners and college financial-aid cells.
solution.moat: Structured cost and outcome data by college and course. Trust is the distribution.

market.tam: ₹1.5 lakh Cr+ education loan book, with private STEM colleges as the pain centre

problems.verdict: Students compare colleges on placement. Nobody compares the loan that pays for it. That gap is the product.

problems.title: Why can't tiffin subscribers customize daily meals?
problems.description: Professionals subscribing to tiffin services receive pre-decided daily menus with no customization options. Dietary preferences, allergies, or taste preferences aren't accommodated. Customers endure dishes they dislike 2-3 times weekly but cannot switch to alternatives within their subscription. Canceling entire subscriptions wastes money on remaining days. No tiffin service allows day-to-day menu selection while maintaining subscription economics.
problems.who: Office workers stuck with dishes they dislike two or three times a week.
problems.pitch: A tiffin subscription with a daily menu you actually choose, dietary filters and swap credits instead of a wasted day.

how: Publish each kitchen's next-day menu by 6 pm and let subscribers pick one of three thalis or a swap credit.
Capture allergies and preferences once, then filter every menu automatically.
Settle with kitchens weekly and route demand to the least-loaded kitchen.
solution.model: Commission per meal plus a subscription fee; kitchen SaaS.
solution.gtm: Office clusters and PG networks; onboard 20 home kitchens in one zone.
solution.moat: A demand-routing network of kitchens with reliable menus.

problems.verdict: Choice is the missing feature in a subscription built on repetition.

problems.title: Why do hospitals hide procedure pricing from patients?
problems.description: Patients admitted for routine procedures or surgeries receive massive bills with line items for consumables, doctor fees, and facility charges that bear no relation to market rates because hospitals don't disclose standardized procedure pricing upfront, leaving patients vulnerable to price gouging during medical emergencies.
problems.who: Patients receiving a ₹2 lakh bill with no idea what was agreed.
problems.pitch: Standard procedure prices and an itemised pre-admission estimate, plus a bill audit after discharge.

how: Build standard price ranges by procedure, city and hospital tier from actual bills and insurer data.
Generate a pre-admission estimate with consumables, doctor fees and facility charges, signed by the hospital.
Audit the final bill against the estimate and flag unexplained line items for negotiation or insurance review.
mvp: Bill audit checklist and dispute pack
solution.model: Per-estimate fee, insurer partnerships and a share of verified savings.
solution.gtm: Insurers, TPAs and corporate health benefits teams.
solution.moat: Actual bill data by procedure and hospital.

market.tam: ₹10 lakh Cr healthcare spend; price opacity a systemic pain

problems.verdict: The bill arrives after the leverage is gone; the estimate arrives before.

problems.title: Why do households lack emergency backup services when domestic help quits suddenly?
problems.description: Households relying on full-time domestic workers for cooking, cleaning, and childcare face sudden crises when their help quits abruptly without serving proper notice periods, leaving working parents scrambling to manage household responsibilities with no emergency backup service providers available.
problems.who: Working couples whose household runs on one domestic worker and collapses when they quit.
problems.pitch: On-call vetted household help for the week your cook disappears — a backup plan, not a full-time hire.

how: Build a pool of verified part-time cooks, cleaners and nannies who want extra shifts.
Sell a standby membership that guarantees a replacement within 24 hours for a defined set of tasks.
Standardise recipes and cleaning checklists so a substitute can step in without a long handover.
mvp: Verified backup pool in two zones
Task checklists and family preferences profile
solution.model: Monthly membership plus per-shift fees when used.
solution.gtm: Apartment WhatsApp groups, HR benefits and existing maid-agency partnerships.
solution.moat: A standby pool large enough to honour the SLA — a density business.

market.tam: ₹20,000 Cr domestic help market; backup is an unserved wedge

problems.verdict: Sell insurance-like peace of mind on top of an informal labour market.

problems.title: Why are CRM systems too complex for 3-person businesses?
problems.description: Micro-businesses with tiny teams cannot adopt traditional customer relationship management software because these platforms are designed for large sales organizations with complex workflows, requiring extensive setup time, expensive subscriptions, and technical expertise that small teams lack, whereas they need simple WhatsApp-based contact management.
problems.who: Micro-businesses that live in WhatsApp and abandon enterprise CRMs in week two.
problems.pitch: A WhatsApp-native CRM for three-person businesses: contacts, follow-ups, quotes and payments, with nothing to configure.

how: Sync WhatsApp conversations into contact cards with a next-action reminder and a simple pipeline.
Add quote creation, payment links and a follow-up sequence that runs inside WhatsApp.
Ship opinionated defaults by trade (interior, tuition, clinic) so setup is a 10-minute import, not a project.
solution.model: Per-seat SaaS with a WhatsApp message pack.
solution.gtm: Trade WhatsApp groups, distributor networks and a free contact-import tool.
solution.moat: Trade-specific templates and conversation data locked into workflows.

problems.verdict: The CRM already exists — it is called WhatsApp, minus the memory.

problems.title: Why can’t hosts prepare restaurant-quality meals at home within 15 minutes?
problems.description: Hosts organizing spontaneous gatherings or last-minute parties struggle to prepare gourmet-quality food within tight timeframes. Shopping for ingredients, marinating proteins, and cooking elaborate dishes takes 3-4 hours minimum. Pre-packaged meal kits available in supermarkets are either unhealthy frozen foods or require extensive cooking time. No premium ready-to-cook gourmet kits exist that deliver restaurant-quality meals in under 15 minutes for home entertaining.
problems.who: Hosts who want to serve something impressive without a three-hour kitchen session.
problems.pitch: Chef-built gourmet kits that go from fridge to plate in 15 minutes, with sauces and sides pre-prepped.

how: Design a menu where the chef does the hard part (marinade, sauce, sous-vide, par-cook) and the host only sears, tosses or plates.
Sell chilled kits with a 15-minute timeline card and a plating photo, portioned for 2 or 4.
Launch on quick commerce for same-evening delivery, with a subscription for weekend hosting.
solution.model: Product margin plus a weekend subscription.
solution.price: ₹599–₹1,299 per kit for two; ₹1,999 for four.
solution.gtm: Instagram food content, hosting communities, and quick-commerce placement before weekends.
solution.moat: Chef recipes engineered for speed and a reliable cold-chain kit format.

market.tam: ₹8,000 Cr ready-to-cook and premium convenience food

problems.verdict: Sell the applause, not the cooking.

problems.title: Why can't patients access digital copies of medical records?
problems.description: Healthcare consumers visiting multiple doctors and specialists must carry physical folders of paper reports, X-ray films, and prescription histories because most hospitals don't provide patients with digital copies of their own medical data, test results, and imaging studies in portable formats.
problems.who: Patients carrying folders of films and reports between specialists.
problems.pitch: Walk into any hospital, walk out with your records digitised — reports, scans and prescriptions in one portable vault.

how: Offer a hospital-desk and home service that scans, OCRs and indexes reports, prescriptions and imaging films.
Structure the data into a searchable timeline and generate a specialist-ready summary.
Share via a secure link with consent and export a print-ready pack.
solution.model: Per-record digitisation fee plus a storage subscription.
solution.gtm: Hospital discharge desks, specialist clinics and home-collection partnerships.
solution.moat: Digitisation operations and structured record data.

problems.verdict: The paper folder is the patient's only current health record.

problems.title: Why do families lose track of wedding gift money?
problems.description: Households lose financial records because traditional cash and envelope-based gifting lacks a digital system to track contributors, amounts, and reciprocity over time.
problems.who: Families hosting weddings who manage cash envelopes and lose the record of reciprocity.
problems.pitch: A gift registry and ledger for Indian weddings — collect digitally, track who gave what, and return the right gift later.

how: Create an event registry with UPI collection, cash-entry logging and a private contributor ledger.
Track amounts, relationships and return-gift status, with reminders for the reciprocal occasions.
Settle to the family's account with a reconciliation report and a guest-facing thank-you flow.
solution.model: Transaction fee on digital gifts plus a premium registry plan.
solution.price: 1.5% on digital gifts; ₹2,999 premium wedding plan.
solution.gtm: Wedding planners, banquet halls and photographers; launch in one wedding-heavy city.
solution.moat: The reciprocity graph, which becomes more useful with every event in a family network.

market.tam: ₹10 lakh Cr+ wedding spend; gifts a large cash segment

problems.verdict: Indian weddings run on reciprocity; nobody keeps the ledger.

problems.title: Why must students commit to expensive annual subscriptions before testing exam platforms?
problems.description: Students wanting to try online learning platforms for exam preparation discover that most services require upfront annual subscription commitments with non-refundable payments, offering no flexibility for pay-per-topic access, course-switching, or trial periods that let students test teaching quality before major financial commitments.
problems.who: Students unwilling to bet ₹12,000 on a platform before knowing if the teaching works.
problems.pitch: Pay for the topic you are stuck on, not the year — micro-access to exam prep with a refundable first lesson.

how: Split courses into topic packs with a 20-minute preview and a single-topic purchase.
Give every purchase a 24-hour refund window and let students stack packs into a full course at a capped total.
Let teachers publish topic packs and keep 70% of revenue.
solution.model: 30% marketplace take rate; institution licences.
solution.price: ₹99–₹499 per topic pack; cap at ₹4,999 per full course.
solution.gtm: Teacher creators on YouTube, exam-season campaigns, and a free doubt-solving community.
solution.moat: Creator supply and topic-level demand data.

problems.verdict: Commitment is the enemy of the first purchase.

problems.title: Why can't anxious people find trustworthy non-prescription sleep solutions easily?
problems.description: Google, melatonin gummies and a ten-minute doctor visit that ends with a prescription. CBT-I is the gold standard but scarce and expensive. OTC options are unregulated, and no one follows up on whether they work.
problems.who: Anxious urban adults aged 25–45 with chronic insomnia who want help without a psychiatric label.
problems.pitch: A pharmacist-led, non-prescription sleep clinic for people who do not want another sedative.

how: Deliver a structured six-week CBT-I programme with a sleep coach and weekly adherence check-ins.
Partner with pharmacies for validated melatonin and supplement protocols, with clear red-flag screening.
Close the loop with wearable sleep data and escalate to a sleep physician when symptoms suggest apnoea or depression.
mvp: Ten pharmacy partners and an outcome registry
solution.model: Programme fee, pharmacy margin, employer wellness contracts.
solution.gtm: Pharmacy counters, mental-health platforms and insomnia communities.
solution.moat: Clinical protocol and outcomes registry. Trust, not technology, is the defensible asset.

risks: Low perceived severity until it becomes chronic

market.tam: ₹3,000 Cr+ sleep-aid market, with a large untreated behavioural segment

problems.verdict: People are already self-medicating. Give them a credible protocol before they graduate to prescriptions.

problems.title: Why can't users redeem credit card reward points easily?
problems.description: Credit card holders accumulate thousands of reward points but struggle to redeem them effectively. Redemption portals have limited inventory, inflated prices, or products worth 30-40% less than point value. Conversion to cash or statement credit has poor rates. Points expire without notification. Users cannot compare redemption value across categories or find optimal use of accumulated rewards.
problems.who: Cardholders sitting on 50,000 points and redeeming them for a 30% haircut.
problems.pitch: See what every reward point is actually worth, across redemption options, transfer partners and expiry dates.

how: Aggregate reward balances and redemption catalogues across major issuers, normalising value per point.
Rank options by effective rupee value, flag poor-value redemptions and alert before points expire.
Guide the transfer to airline/hotel partners when that yields more value, with a step-by-step flow.
solution.model: Affiliate revenue from partners and a premium subscription.
solution.gtm: Credit-card communities and personal-finance creators; publish a monthly 'best redemption' index.
solution.moat: Continuously updated redemption catalogue and valuation data.

problems.verdict: Points are a currency with no price tag — until someone publishes one.

problems.title: Why are pest control treatments ineffective within months?
problems.description: Households paying ₹3,000-8,000 for cockroach or termite treatment discover pests return within 3-6 months despite service warranties. Companies blame customers for cleanliness. Warranty claims require extensive proof. Re-treatment isn't provided. No performance-based pest control with guaranteed results exists.
problems.who: Households that paid ₹5,000 and saw cockroaches return in three months.
problems.pitch: Performance-based pest control: you pay for the result, with free re-treatment until the infestation stays gone.

how: Sell a 12-month outcome contract with scheduled follow-ups at 30, 90 and 180 days, not a one-time spray.
Use a documented treatment plan per pest with gel-bait and proofing, and log stations and active ingredients.
Re-treat free within the warranty period; publish a customer-visible service log.
solution.model: Annual contract paid monthly; commercial contracts for restaurants and societies.
solution.gtm: Housing societies, restaurants and paediatric clinics; lead with the warranty.
solution.moat: Outcome data by pest and building type, plus a trained technician bench.

problems.verdict: Shift the risk to the operator and the incentives fix themselves.

problems.title: Why do appliance repair shops not provide warranties?
problems.description: Customers getting washing machines, refrigerators, or microwaves repaired at local shops receive no warranty on repair work or replacement parts. If the same issue recurs within days, customers must pay again. Unauthorized service centers use duplicate parts without guarantees. No accountability exists for repair quality.
problems.who: Customers whose washing machine failed again a week after a ₹2,500 repair.
problems.pitch: A repair warranty network: vetted local shops, genuine parts and a six-month guarantee backed by a claims fund.

how: Onboard repair shops with parts sourcing checks and a standard six-month workmanship warranty.
Register every repair with a parts list and invoice in a customer wallet, and fund claims from a small per-job premium.
Send a replacement technician if the original shop cannot fix a valid claim.
mvp: Claims fund and backup technician pool
solution.model: Warranty premium per repair plus shop subscription.
solution.gtm: Local repair markets, appliance resale shops, and a WhatsApp warranty card customers can show.
solution.moat: Claims data on which shops and parts fail.

problems.verdict: Warranty is how an informal market becomes accountable.

problems.title: Why don't consumers trust pre-ground masala powder quality?
problems.description: Home cooks suspicious of store-bought spice powders worry about adulteration, stale grinding, or artificial colors and preservatives added by manufacturers. Grinding spices at home ensures freshness but requires buying whole spices, owning a grinder, and spending time daily. No service offers custom whole-spice-to-fresh-ground delivery where consumers select spices and receive freshly ground powders within hours.
problems.who: Home cooks who distrust packaged masala but do not want to grind daily.
problems.pitch: Choose whole spices, get them freshly ground and delivered the same day, with a batch and purity report.

how: Let customers pick a blend or a standard mix from whole spices, ground to order in small batches.
Print the grind date, spice origin and a purity check on every pack, and ship within hours.
Offer a monthly 'fresh grind' subscription timed to household consumption.
mvp: Six standard blends plus custom mix
solution.model: Product margin plus a subscription.
solution.gtm: Local food creators, WhatsApp order groups, and premium grocery shelves.
solution.moat: Freshness supply chain and a custom-blend recipe library.

market.tam: ₹25,000 Cr spices; freshness a premium wedge

problems.verdict: Freshness is a date stamp customers can verify.

problems.title: Why do apartment maintenance payments lack itemized breakdowns?
problems.description: Residents paying monthly society maintenance fees (₹3,000-10,000) receive no itemized breakdown of where money is spent. Lump sum amounts are collected without transparency on staff salaries, repair costs, utilities, or reserve fund allocation. Digital payment receipts just show 'maintenance' without expense categories. Residents cannot verify if charges are justified or question specific expense increases without detailed financial reporting.
problems.who: Residents paying ₹3,000–10,000 a month with no idea where it goes; committee treasurers drowning in spreadsheets.
problems.pitch: Itemised maintenance billing for housing societies, with vendor bills, expense categories and a resident-facing ledger.

how: Give the treasurer a billing module with heads (security, housekeeping, utilities, sinking fund) and vendor invoice uploads.
Publish a resident ledger with the month's breakdown, variance against budget and reserve fund balance.
Collect maintenance via UPI with auto-reconciliation and overdue reminders.
solution.model: ₹25–₹60 per flat per month; implementation fee for large societies.
solution.gtm: Society committees, facility managers and apartment federations.
solution.moat: Society-level financial history and committee switching costs.

problems.verdict: Transparency is a treasurer's best defence.

problems.title: Why can’t small restaurants access wholesale ingredient pricing without large minimum orders?
problems.description: Independent restaurants and small food establishments cannot access the same cost-effective wholesale pricing that larger chains enjoy because suppliers impose minimum order quantities that exceed their storage capacity and demand, forcing them to buy from retail distributors at significantly higher per-unit costs.
problems.who: Independent cafés, cloud kitchens and small restaurants buying 20–40 ingredients a week.
problems.pitch: Wholesale ingredient buying for small restaurants, without the 100 kg minimum.

how: Pool orders across nearby kitchens to unlock wholesale prices without each kitchen meeting the MOQ.
Run a cold-chain last mile with transparent live pricing and next-morning delivery windows.
Add standing orders, credit terms and spoilage-aware forecasting so kitchens order less, more often.
solution.model: Product margin, delivery fee, supplier promotions.
solution.gtm: Cloud-kitchen hubs, chef communities and distributor partnerships for sourcing.
solution.moat: Pooled demand density and spoilage data. Density is everything in perishables.

market.tam: ₹40,000 Cr+ restaurant food supply, with 1 lakh+ small kitchens

problems.verdict: Small kitchens do not need cheaper food as much as they need to stop over-ordering it.

problems.title: Why do diners waste time waiting for restaurant tables?
problems.description: Customers visiting popular restaurants during peak hours face 30-60 minute waits for tables without knowing exact wait times. Restaurant staff provide vague estimates. Customers cannot join virtual queues remotely or pre-order while waiting. Walking to another restaurant risks encountering similar waits. No real-time restaurant queue visibility system allows diners to make informed decisions or pre-order food before being seated.
problems.who: Diners burning 45 minutes outside a popular restaurant on a Saturday.
problems.pitch: Join a restaurant's real queue remotely, see the actual wait and pre-order so the food lands when you sit.

how: Give restaurants a table-turn tracker that produces a real wait estimate from seating history, not staff guesses.
Let diners join the queue from Maps/Instagram, pre-order, and get a 10-minute warning.
Sell the host-stand dashboard and take a small fee on pre-orders.
solution.model: Restaurant SaaS plus a commission on pre-ordered meals.
solution.gtm: Start with 30 high-wait casual dining outlets in one city; publish live wait times for consumers.
solution.moat: Table-turn data and diner demand captured before arrival.

market.tam: ₹4,000 Cr organised dining; wait management a wedge

problems.verdict: The queue is a data product hiding in a host stand.

problems.title: Why can’t households schedule doorstep e-waste pickup with instant rewards?
problems.description: Households accumulating old phones, laptops, batteries, and chargers cannot find convenient e-waste collection points. Items end up in regular trash. No incentive or bounty programs exist for proper disposal. E-waste awareness is low.
problems.who: Households hoarding old phones and laptops because disposal is inconvenient.
problems.pitch: Doorstep e-waste pickup with instant UPI rewards, certified recycling and proof of data destruction.

how: Quote an instant value from a photo and model, then schedule a doorstep pickup with a weighing scale.
Pay instantly via UPI and route devices to certified refurbishers or recyclers.
Issue a data-destruction certificate for storage devices and a recycling certificate for the household.
solution.model: Refurbishment margin, recycler fees and brand take-back contracts.
solution.gtm: Apartment societies, office IT asset disposal and brand take-back programmes.
solution.moat: Certified recycling chain and household pickup density.

problems.verdict: Make disposal pay better than the drawer.

problems.title: Why can't small shippers access bulk shipping discounts?
problems.description: Small online sellers shipping 50-200 orders monthly pay retail courier rates while large sellers get 40-50% discounts for 1,000+ shipments. No platform aggregates small sellers for collective bargaining. Per-shipment costs are ₹20-30 higher, destroying competitiveness.
problems.who: Small online sellers paying retail rates while larger competitors pay 40–50% less.
problems.pitch: Pool small sellers into one negotiated courier contract, so 100 shipments a month get 1,000-shipment rates.

how: Aggregate members' volumes under a single master contract and allocate pooled rates by usage.
Provide one pickup and one label flow, with a shared wallet and transparent per-shipment billing.
Use the pool's volume to negotiate regional courier rates and pass most of the discount through.
mvp: Master courier contracts in three zones
solution.model: 3–5% platform fee on pooled shipping spend.
solution.price: Free to join; discount of 20–35% versus retail.
solution.gtm: Seller WhatsApp groups, export clusters and e-commerce meetups.
solution.moat: Aggregated volume and courier contracts.

problems.verdict: Small sellers do not need a courier; they need a buyer with leverage.

problems.title: How do societies manage monsoon waterlogging prevention?
problems.description: Residential areas face repeated waterlogging during monsoons due to clogged drains. Citizens report issues but municipal action is slow. No preventive drain cleaning happens. Communities cannot crowdsource drain clearing or get real-time waterlogging alerts for route planning.
problems.who: Residents wading through knee-deep water because drains were never cleaned.
problems.pitch: Pre-monsoon drain audits, crowdsourced waterlogging reports and live alerts for the routes societies use daily.

how: Audit and photograph every drain in a ward before monsoon, with a cleaning status and a responsible contractor.
Collect resident reports with photos and GPS, and cluster them into a live waterlogging map.
Sell the audit and alert layer to municipalities and societies, and publish a ward readiness score.
solution.model: Municipal contracts and society subscriptions; CSR funding.
solution.gtm: RWAs, ward councillors and municipal stormwater departments.
solution.moat: Ward-level drain condition data and resident reports.

problems.verdict: Waterlogging is predictable; the data just arrives too late.

problems.title: Why do office workers resort to unhealthy afternoon snacks?
problems.description: Office professionals experiencing 4 PM hunger pangs resort to unhealthy snacks like samosas, biscuits, or chips from nearby cafeterias due to lack of healthy alternatives. Meal subscriptions deliver only lunch and dinner. Carrying healthy snacks from home isn't practical daily. No service delivers portion-controlled healthy snack boxes to offices timed for afternoon hunger, filling the gap between lunch and dinner.
problems.who: Office workers hitting the samosa-and-biscuit slump; HR teams buying wellness perks.
problems.pitch: A portion-controlled healthy snack box delivered to offices at 4 pm, priced per seat.

how: Design a rotating 21-snack menu with under-150-calorie portions, protein and fibre targets, and no repeat within two weeks.
Deliver to an office pantry in a single crate by 3:45 pm, with individual named portions.
Bill per employee per month and report consumption and nutrition to HR.
solution.model: Per-seat monthly subscription; office pantry contracts.
solution.gtm: HR wellness budgets and office-admin communities; pilot in two tech parks.
solution.moat: Office route density and a proven menu rotation.

market.tam: ₹3,000 Cr office pantry and corporate wellness

problems.verdict: Sell to the employer's wellness budget, deliver to the employee's 4 pm.

problems.title: Is there a way for businesses collect quick customer feedback beyond surveys?
problems.description: Local service businesses receive minimal customer feedback because traditional lengthy online surveys have poor completion rates, and they need interactive audio-based feedback systems that let customers record 5-second voice reviews immediately after service delivery, making input effortless and increasing response rates dramatically.
problems.who: Local service businesses that get three survey responses a year.
problems.pitch: A five-second voice review at the counter — the customer speaks, the owner gets a sentiment score and a clip.

how: Put a QR at the counter or checkout; the customer records a five-second voice note with one tap, no login.
Transcribe and score sentiment and themes, then surface the clips that need the owner's attention.
Route negative feedback to a recovery workflow and positive clips to the business's Google reviews.
solution.model: Per-location monthly SaaS.
solution.gtm: Restaurants, salons and clinics; sell through POS and Google-review agencies.
solution.moat: Voice feedback corpus and recovery playbooks.

market.tam: ₹1,500 Cr SMB feedback and reputation tools

problems.verdict: A five-second voice note beats a twelve-question survey every time.

problems.title: Why can’t reverse logistics be dynamically priced like forward shipping?
problems.description: Product returns, warranty replacements, and rejected deliveries cost 30-40% more than forward shipping. Couriers charge premiums for reverse pickup. Small businesses cannot negotiate reverse logistics rates. High reverse logistics costs eat into thin margins on returned products.
problems.who: D2C brands and small sellers whose return costs eat their margin.
problems.pitch: Dynamic reverse-pickup pricing that batches returns by pincode so small sellers stop paying a 35% premium.

how: Aggregate reverse pickups by pincode and time window, then auction the route to nearby couriers.
Price each pickup from distance, batch density and courier capacity, and pass the saving through.
Grade returns at pickup so the seller knows resale, refurbish or scrap before it reaches the warehouse.
solution.model: Per-pickup fee plus a share of the savings versus standard reverse rates.
solution.gtm: D2C brands with return rates above 10%, plus marketplace reverse-logistics contracts.
solution.moat: Pincode-level batch density.

problems.verdict: Density is the discount.

problems.title: Why can't consumers see verified kitchen safety standards on food delivery apps?
problems.description: A 4.2-star rating, styled food photos and an FSSAI number nobody checks. Platforms rate taste and speed, not safety. Audits are annual paper exercises and inspection reports are not public.
problems.who: Urban customers ordering four to ten times a month, and cloud kitchens with no brand to protect.
problems.pitch: A verified hygiene layer for food delivery: audits, live kitchen evidence and insurance behind every order.

how: Run unannounced audits with photo and video evidence, ATP surface swabs and cold-chain checks.
Publish a hygiene score inside listings through partner APIs, with an open-kitchen camera badge for top performers.
Attach order-level cover from an insurance partner, so a bad meal has a claims path.
mvp: Audit protocol and 100-kitchen pilot in one city
One aggregator pilot and an insurance partner
solution.model: Kitchen subscriptions, platform audit fees, insurance commission.
solution.price: ₹2,999/month per kitchen. Audit fees from platforms.
solution.gtm: Start with cloud-kitchen operators and premium brands. Publish a city hygiene index to earn attention.
solution.moat: A standard, an audit network and historical evidence. Diners create the pull.

market.tam: India's ₹80,000 Cr+ food delivery market, with 1 lakh+ cloud kitchens

problems.verdict: Every food order is a trust decision. The rating is the wrong instrument; an audit score is the right one.

problems.title: Why do AC installation charges vary unpredictably?
problems.description: Customers purchasing air conditioners discover installation costs vary from ₹2,000 to ₹8,000 for the same work depending on technician. Additional charges for copper piping, brackets, or electrical work surprise customers. Dealers and brands don't provide installation cost estimates upfront. No transparent AC installation pricing standards exist.
problems.who: Buyers surprised by ₹2,000–₹8,000 installation quotes for identical work.
problems.pitch: A fixed, itemised AC installation price by unit type and site condition — before the box is opened.

how: Publish a price table by tonnage, split/window, pipe length, bracket type and floor access.
Certify installers on a checklist covering vacuuming, leak test and drainage slope, with photo proof.
Offer a 90-day installation warranty and handle brand warranty paperwork.
solution.model: Fixed installation fee plus a certification margin; brand partnerships.
solution.gtm: Electronics retailers and AC brands that want to stop installation complaints.
solution.moat: Certified installer coverage and brand referral agreements.

problems.verdict: The surprise is the product problem.

problems.title: How do consumers verify cold chain integrity?
problems.description: Customers ordering ice cream, frozen foods, or temperature-sensitive products through delivery apps receive items that show signs of melting and refreezing, indicating cold chain breaks during transportation. Delivery partners lack refrigerated vehicles or insulated containers. Consumers cannot verify whether products maintained required temperatures throughout the journey. Complaints to platforms are difficult to prove without evidence, leaving customers with compromised food safety and quality.
problems.who: Ice-cream and frozen-food buyers; platforms fielding unprovable complaints.
problems.pitch: A ₹15 temperature logger and QR proof on every frozen delivery, so a melted tub is evidence, not an argument.

how: Attach a single-use time-temperature indicator to the pack at dispatch and bind it to the order QR.
Let the customer scan on delivery to see whether the cold chain held, and auto-approve a refund if it did not.
Feed breach data back to the dark store and delivery route to fix the worst legs.
solution.model: Per-indicator fee plus a platform analytics subscription.
solution.gtm: Start with one ice-cream brand and one quick-commerce dark store.
solution.moat: Cold-chain breach data by route and pack type.

market.tam: ₹15,000 Cr frozen and chilled food; spoilage a measurable cost

problems.verdict: Make the invisible cold chain visible at the doorstep.

problems.title: How do customers book electricians for small jobs?
problems.description: Homeowners needing fan installation, switchboard replacement, or light fixture changes cannot find electricians willing to take small jobs. Most electricians prefer full rewiring contracts. Per-point charging varies wildly (₹200-800 per point). Booking for specific time slots is impossible. No platform aggregates electricians for small electrical work.
problems.who: Homeowners with five small electrical jobs and no electrician willing to come.
problems.pitch: Fixed-price electrical points — fan, switchboard, light — booked in a two-hour slot, no full-rewiring contract required.

how: Publish a per-point price list with a 30-minute minimum and a two-hour arrival window.
Recruit electricians and fill their idle time between large contracts with small jobs.
Add a safety checklist and a 30-day workmanship guarantee per point.
solution.model: Per-job commission plus a materials margin; society annual contracts.
solution.price: ₹199–₹499 per point; ₹99 visit fee waived on booking.
solution.gtm: Apartment societies, hardware stores and landlord groups.
solution.moat: Electrician density and a fixed-price brand for tiny jobs.

problems.verdict: Small jobs are a scheduling problem, not a demand problem.

problems.title: Why can't businesses compare courier rates easily?
problems.description: E-commerce sellers must manually check rates across 5-10 courier companies for each shipment. Rate cards have complex zone-based, weight-based, and volumetric pricing. No real-time rate aggregator exists. Businesses waste 30-60 minutes daily on rate comparison, often choosing suboptimal couriers.
problems.who: E-commerce sellers wasting an hour a day checking five courier portals.
problems.pitch: One screen that compares live courier rates by pincode, weight and service level, then books the label.

how: Ingest rate cards and serviceability from major and regional couriers, normalising zone, weight and volumetric rules.
Show the true cost per shipment including RTO risk, then book and print the label in one click.
Track performance by courier and auto-route future shipments to the best combination of cost and delivery rate.
solution.model: Per-label booking fee plus a SaaS tier.
solution.gtm: Seller communities, e-commerce enablers and 3PL consultants.
solution.moat: Normalised rate and performance data across couriers.

problems.verdict: The rate card is the product; the booking is the habit.

problems.title: Why can’t pet owners find trusted home-stay alternatives to boarding kennels?
problems.description: Dog and cat owners dreading business trips or vacations avoid traditional pet boarding kennels where animals are confined to small cages for extended periods and instead seek verified networks of local pet-loving families who can provide home-stay arrangements where pets roam freely in family environments.
problems.who: Pet owners travelling for work or holidays who refuse kennels.
problems.pitch: Verified home boarding for pets — a real family home, daily photo updates and insurance, instead of a cage.

how: Certify host homes with a safety audit, pet-free-of-hazards checklist and a meet-and-greet before booking.
Match by pet temperament, size and medical needs; require vaccination records and a vet-on-call tie-up.
Send scheduled photo/video updates and a daily wellbeing log; include emergency vet cover.
mvp: Daily update feed and vet hotline
solution.model: 20% commission per night; host certification fee; insurance attach.
solution.gtm: Vet clinics, pet-grooming salons and breed-specific communities; content on kennel alternatives.
solution.moat: Audited host supply and repeat trust with pet parents.

market.tam: ₹2,000 Cr pet services, boarding growing fast

problems.verdict: Pet parents pay for peace of mind, not square footage.

problems.title: Why do valet customers lack car parking visibility?
problems.description: Customers using valet parking services at shopping centers and restaurants experience anxiety about the security and treatment of their vehicles because they receive no transparency about actual parking locations, cannot monitor their cars remotely, and hear stories of valets taking vehicles for unauthorized personal use.
problems.who: Malls, restaurants and hotels running valet; customers anxious about where their car went.
problems.pitch: A valet operations layer with photo check-in, geofenced parking and live car status for the customer.

how: Issue a digital valet ticket with four-corner photos, odometer and fuel level at handover.
Track the parked location by geofence and surface 'parked / requested / arriving' status to the customer.
Flag unauthorized movement with a geofence alert and keep a timestamped chain of custody.
solution.model: Per-venue SaaS plus a per-transaction fee.
solution.gtm: Sell to mall operators and restaurant groups; pilot at two high-volume venues and use damage-claim reduction as the ROI story.
solution.moat: Venue contracts and the audit trail that becomes the liability shield.

risks: Low willingness to pay outside premium venues
problems.verdict: Liability reduction is an easier sale than customer delight.

problems.title: Why do hair color treatments damage hair despite salon promises?
problems.description: Customers getting hair coloring, highlighting, or balayage services at salons experience severe hair damage - dryness, breakage, and texture loss - within 2-3 weeks despite salons promising 'no damage' formulas. Salons use harsh bleaching agents to achieve desired colors quickly rather than gentler multi-session processes. Post-color care product recommendations are expensive (₹2,000-5,000 for shampoos and serums). No salon offers damage-free guarantees with refunds or corrective treatments, leaving customers with damaged hair and ₹3,000-8,000 sunk costs per service.
problems.who: Clients spending ₹3,000–8,000 on colour who end up with breakage; salons losing repeat visits to damage complaints.
problems.pitch: A colour service with a strand test, staged lightening and an eight-week damage guarantee — sold as a salon certification.

how: Mandate a strand test and hair-health score before any bleach, with a staged two-session protocol for dark-to-light lifts.
Bundle bond-builder treatment into the service price and a low-cost aftercare kit, instead of upselling ₹3,000 serums.
Back the service with an eight-week breakage guarantee: free corrective treatment or a partial refund.
solution.model: Certification and audit fees from salons, plus aftercare product margin.
solution.gtm: Sell to premium salons as a damage-reduction standard; consumers search for 'guaranteed hair colour'.
solution.moat: A published protocol and guarantee that a discount salon cannot credibly copy.

problems.verdict: A guarantee forces the protocol — and the protocol is the moat.

problems.title: Why can't renters access verified mold, pests or hazards before signing leases?
problems.description: A hurried visit, a broker's assurance and a 'no dampness' clause. Mould shows up after the first monsoon. Inspections are one-off, undocumented and unenforceable. The landlord controls the evidence and the deposit.
problems.who: Renters in metros signing 11-month leases, especially first-time movers and families with children.
problems.pitch: Move-in health checks and hazard records that renters can actually trust before signing.

how: Send a certified inspector with a moisture meter, mould swabs and a pest checklist to produce a 30-point health report before the lease.
Attach the report to the rental agreement as a baseline, with photo evidence and remediation cost estimates.
Offer a 30-day re-check and a verified-landlord badge that future tenants can see.
mvp: Certified inspector network in two cities
Shareable report link plus landlord onboarding
solution.model: Renter-paid inspection, landlord verification subscription, property-manager contracts.
solution.price: ₹999–1,999 per inspection. ₹499/month for a verified-landlord badge.
solution.gtm: Broker partnerships, apartment associations and rental communities. Use the city hazard index as a PR hook.
solution.moat: Standardised building-level hazard data and an inspector network. Difficult to copy without local operations.

risks: Low willingness to pay before a lease

market.tam: India's urban rental market, with 30 crore+ renters and no standard move-in health record

problems.verdict: Renters already pay a deposit to protect the landlord. A small fee to protect their health is an easy story.

problems.title: Why is specialized care missing for silk, embroidery and designer clothing?
problems.description: Consumers owning premium fabrics like silk sarees, designer suits, and delicate embroidered clothing frequently have these expensive items damaged or destroyed by neighborhood dry cleaners who use aggressive chemical solvents and lack specialized knowledge about treating different fabric types with appropriate gentle cleaning methods.
problems.who: Owners of ₹15,000-plus sarees, lehengas and suits who have lost a garment to a neighbourhood dry cleaner.
problems.pitch: Specialist cleaning for silk, embroidery and designer wear, with fabric-specific protocols, photo documentation and insurance.

how: Tag each garment by fabric, embellishment and colour-fastness, then route to a protocol (solvent, hand-finish, no-spin).
Photograph before and after, flag pre-existing damage, and insure each piece up to a declared value.
Offer doorstep pickup in a garment box, a 5–7 day turnaround, and a rewash guarantee.
solution.model: Per-garment cleaning fee, restoration services, and seasonal storage subscriptions.
solution.gtm: Partnerships with bridal boutiques, designer stores and tailor shops; trust content on fabric care.
solution.moat: Protocol knowledge, trained finishers and insurance-backed trust.

problems.verdict: Premium garments need a specialist, not a faster dry cleaner.

problems.title: How do home painters quote prices without hidden costs?
problems.description: Customers hiring painters for home renovation receive initial low quotes but face cost escalations during work for primer, putty, labor extras, or material quality upgrades. Final bills exceed estimates by 40-60%. No standardized pricing exists. Customers cannot compare quotes transparently or lock-in final costs before work begins.
problems.who: Homeowners hit with a 40–60% escalation after a low initial quote.
problems.pitch: A measured, itemised painting quote with a locked price, material spec and milestone payments.

how: Measure rooms on-site or from a floor plan, then generate a line-item quote covering putty, primer, coats and labour.
Lock the price for 30 days and specify brand and grade per coat, with photo evidence at each stage.
Release payment in milestones after inspection, holding 10% for 30 days.
solution.model: Fixed 8–10% platform fee on the contracted job; painter network.
solution.price: ₹18–₹32 per sq ft all-in; platform fee included.
solution.gtm: Apartment repainting cycles, real-estate handover agents and painter crew partnerships.
solution.moat: A pricing dataset by city and surface condition plus a vetted painter bench.

problems.verdict: A quote is only useful if it cannot move.

problems.title: Why are small retailers forced into distributor margins without direct brand access?
problems.description: Small retailers operating on thin margins find themselves trapped in traditional distribution chains where intermediaries and distributors capture 40-50% of potential profits because retailers lack the connections, minimum order quantities, or platforms to source products directly from brands and manufacturers.
problems.who: Neighbourhood retailers and emerging D2C brands trying to reach them.
problems.pitch: Direct brand-to-retailer ordering with transparent margins and next-day replenishment.

how: Give retailers one ordering app with brand catalogues, landed prices and transparent margins.
Aggregate last-mile delivery through existing distributors instead of duplicating their trucks.
Send sell-through data back to brands so they can plan production and targeted offers.
mvp: 200 retailers and 15 brands in one city
solution.model: Take rate on orders, brand data subscriptions, credit referral.
solution.gtm: Retail associations, brand sales teams and distributor partnerships.
solution.moat: Retailer density and brand sell-through data.

market.tam: ₹80 lakh Cr+ retail distribution, with 1.2 crore kirana stores

problems.verdict: The distributor is not the enemy; the opaque margin is. Sell transparency and reliability together.

problems.title: Why do people leaving formal education lack structure, mentorship and clear career guidance?
problems.description: A placement cell that disappears after graduation, YouTube advice and hundreds of cold applications. Guidance is either expensive one-on-one counselling or generic content. Nobody is accountable for the outcome.
problems.who: Graduates of tier-2 and tier-3 colleges, plus dropouts entering the workforce for the first time.
problems.pitch: A career operating system for the 18–24s who leave education without a map.

how: Run an eight-week cohort with a personal career map, weekly mentor sessions and one real portfolio project.
Issue employer-verified skill badges and route graduates into hiring partners with a warm introduction.
Keep alumni pods by city and role so the network survives the cohort.
solution.model: Cohort fee with an income-share option, employer hiring fees, college B2B contracts.
solution.price: ₹9,999 per cohort. Colleges pay ₹1,500 per student for placement support.
