solution.gtm: College placement cells, YouTube creators and referral loops from alumni.
solution.moat: Outcome data and employer trust. Thin without scale, so pick one role and own it.

market.tam: 1.5 crore+ graduates a year, with tier-2/3 employability as the gap

problems.verdict: Degrees are getting cheaper to obtain and more expensive to use. Sell the bridge, not another course.

problems.title: Why do appliance technicians overcharge for parts and inspections?
problems.description: Homeowners needing repairs for washing machines, refrigerators, or air conditioners feel trapped and exploited when service technicians charge substantial upfront "inspection fees" just for diagnosis and then provide inflated quotations for replacement parts, knowing desperate customers have few alternatives.
problems.who: Households quoted ₹4,500 for a ₹900 part, with no way to verify.
problems.pitch: Transparent appliance repair with a capped diagnosis fee, a public parts price index and payment released only after the fix works.

how: Publish a parts price index by model and a fixed diagnosis fee that is waived if the repair is booked.
Send a verified technician who logs the fault code and part number in-app; the customer approves the quote before work starts.
Hold payment in escrow for 48 hours and require a 90-day repair warranty.
mvp: Parts price database for top 20 appliance models
solution.model: Fixed service fee plus parts margin; extended warranty plans.
solution.gtm: SEO on error codes and model numbers, plus society service camps.
solution.moat: A proprietary parts-price and failure dataset that makes quotes credible.

problems.verdict: Price transparency is the product; escrow makes it enforceable.

problems.title: Why isn’t fragile-handling monitored with sensors and chain-of-custody tech?
problems.description: Sellers shipping electronics, glassware, or ceramics face 10-15% damage rates. Fragile stickers are ignored by handlers. Businesses cannot mandate special handling. Insurance claims are tedious. No courier guarantees fragile item safety with damage-free delivery assurance.
problems.who: Sellers shipping electronics, glassware and ceramics with 10–15% damage rates.
problems.pitch: A shock-and-tilt sensor with a chain-of-custody seal that proves whether a fragile parcel was mishandled.

how: Ship a reusable shock/tilt logger inside the package that records the worst impact and timestamps it.
Bind the sensor to the parcel's scan trail so a damage claim shows exactly which hop caused it.
Offer a damage-free guarantee: refund or replace if the logger proves mishandling.
solution.model: Per-shipment sensor rental plus a guarantee premium.
solution.price: ₹25–₹60 per shipment; guarantee from 0.8% of value.
solution.gtm: Premium electronics and decor sellers; prove damage reduction over 1,000 parcels.
solution.moat: Mishandling data by courier and route.

market.tam: ₹4,000 Cr fragile shipping; damage a direct cost

problems.verdict: Fragile stickers are a request; sensors are evidence.

problems.title: How can affordable cybersecurity checks be made accessible to small businesses?
problems.description: Small enterprises operating e-commerce sites or company websites lack cybersecurity budgets and technical expertise to monitor for vulnerabilities, malware injections, or data breaches, and they need simple one-click security audit tools that automatically scan for common threats and provide plain-language alerts.
problems.who: SMEs running a storefront with no security team and no budget for a pentest.
problems.pitch: A one-click security audit for small business websites, with plain-language fixes and continuous monitoring.

how: Scan for exposed admin panels, outdated plugins, missing headers, leaked credentials and malware signatures.
Translate findings into a prioritised fix list with copy-paste instructions for Shopify, WordPress and custom sites.
Monitor continuously and alert on new exposures, with a monthly compliance certificate.
solution.model: Tiered monthly subscription plus remediation services.
solution.gtm: Web agencies, hosting providers and e-commerce seller communities.
solution.moat: Scan coverage and remediation playbooks.

problems.verdict: Small businesses do not need a pentest; they need the five things to fix today.

problems.title: How can data flow seamlessly between Excel, CRM, and invoicing systems?
problems.description: SMEs operating with fragmented software tools waste significant administrative time manually transferring customer data from spreadsheets to CRM systems, copying invoices to accounting software, and re-entering information across platforms because affordable no-code integration connectors that can automate data syncing don't exist.
problems.who: SMEs where a staff member copies rows between spreadsheets, Zoho and Tally every day.
problems.pitch: No-code connectors that keep Excel, CRM, invoicing and payments in sync for Indian SME stacks.

how: Ship prebuilt connectors for the ten tools Indian SMEs actually use, with field mapping and dedupe rules.
Run syncs on a schedule or webhook, with a conflict log that a non-technical owner can resolve.
Add templates for common flows: lead to CRM, invoice to Tally, payment to ledger.
mvp: Five connectors and a mapping UI
solution.model: Per-connection monthly fee plus implementation services.
solution.gtm: CA firms and implementation partners who already configure Tally and Zoho.
solution.moat: Connector coverage and partner distribution.

problems.verdict: SMEs do not need APIs; they need the copy-paste to stop.

problems.title: Why can't shops see real-time supplier stock levels?
problems.description: Small shop owners constantly face inventory mismanagement issues because they cannot see real-time stock levels or availability from their upstream suppliers, leading to either excessive over-ordering that ties up working capital or frustrating stockouts that result in lost sales.
problems.who: Kirana and specialty retailers ordering from 10–20 distributors.
problems.pitch: Live supplier stock levels for small shops, without asking 'bhaiya, hai kya?'

how: Integrate with distributor POS and ERP systems to publish live availability and batch-level stock.
Let retailers order on WhatsApp with substitute suggestions when an SKU is short.
Add demand forecasting and auto-replenishment for the top 100 SKUs.
solution.model: Retailer SaaS, distributor subscription, fulfilment fee.
solution.price: ₹499–999/month per retailer. Distributors pay for demand analytics.
solution.gtm: Distributor networks and retail associations in one city.
solution.moat: Distributor integrations are tedious and sticky. Build the boring pipe.

market.tam: 12 million+ retail outlets and their distributor networks

problems.verdict: A stockout is a customer lost to the shop next door. Sell certainty, not software.

problems.title: Why do micro-SMEs waste 10+ hours weekly on invoice management?
problems.description: Micro and small businesses waste significant administrative time creating, tracking, and reconciling invoices manually because enterprise-grade ERP systems are prohibitively expensive, overly complex for their simple needs, and require extensive training that small teams cannot afford.
problems.who: Micro-SME owners with 1–20 employees and no dedicated finance hire.
problems.pitch: Accounts payable on WhatsApp: capture invoices, reconcile GST and pay on time.

how: Let the owner forward any invoice to a WhatsApp bot, which extracts vendor, GSTIN, amount and tax.
Validate GST details, route approvals and schedule payment against due dates.
Sync the ledger to Tally or Zoho so the CA works from clean books instead of chasing photos.
solution.model: SaaS subscription, payment float, CA partner revenue share.
solution.gtm: CA firms, GST Suvidha providers and business WhatsApp groups.
solution.moat: Workflow habit plus accountant distribution. Low technical moat, so speed matters.

market.tam: 6 crore+ MSMEs, with 1 crore+ active GST filers

problems.verdict: The best interface for a micro-SME is the one already open. Build inside WhatsApp, not beside it.

problems.title: Why do teachers lack real time mental health support at work?
problems.description: Annual wellness workshops, a helpline nobody calls, and a culture where admitting burnout looks like incompetence. Generic EAPs ignore the school context. Teachers do not trust confidentiality and schools cannot see whether the benefit works.
problems.who: K–12 teachers in private school chains, especially early-career teachers managing 40+ students and parent WhatsApp groups.
problems.pitch: A confidential mental-health benefit built for teachers, delivered in the twenty minutes they actually have.

how: Offer 15-minute video or chat sessions with counsellors trained on classroom stressors, bookable in a free period.
Run anonymous burnout check-ins and give school leaders only aggregate dashboards, never individual data.
Train principals on workload triggers and provide a confidential escalation path for serious cases.
mvp: Aggregate wellbeing dashboard for school leaders
solution.model: Per-teacher monthly fee billed to the school, with a family add-on.
solution.gtm: School chains and teacher unions. Lead with attrition and absence data from two pilot chains.
solution.moat: Context-trained counsellors and school distribution. Weak alone, stronger bundled with HR benefits.

market.tam: 1 crore+ school teachers in India, with private chains as the beachhead

problems.verdict: Teacher burnout is a school retention problem wearing a wellness label. Sell it to the people who lose when teachers quit.

problems.title: Why do skincare products fail in India's humidity and pollution?
problems.description: Consumers investing in premium international skincare brands discover their products underperform or cause skin problems because formulations designed for temperate Western climates don't account for India's extreme humidity levels, high pollution exposure, and intense UV radiation that require region-specific adjustments.
problems.who: Urban Indian consumers who bought imported actives that pill, break down or irritate in 30°C-plus, 80% humidity conditions.
problems.pitch: Skincare formulated and stability-tested for Indian humidity, pollution and UV — with the test data printed on every product.

how: Run a climate-chamber stability programme at 35°C/80% RH and publish texture, pH and actives-retention results per batch.
Design lightweight, film-forming textures and barrier-first actives for polluted, high-UV cities, with a 4-week usage patch test.
Sell a skin-climate diagnostic that maps humidity, pollution and UV exposure to a three-step routine.
mvp: Three SKUs: cleanser, barrier serum, SPF 50 gel
Stability and patch-test reports per batch
solution.model: D2C margin plus a replenishment subscription; later, formulation licensing to other brands.
solution.gtm: Dermatologist and esthetician sampling, climate-data-led content, and quick-commerce listing once repeat rates hold.
solution.moat: Climate-specific clinical data and a formulation library that imported brands cannot claim.

risks: High CAC without a diagnostic wedge

market.tam: ₹20,000 Cr Indian skincare market; climate-fit segment nascent

problems.verdict: Formulation for the actual climate is a defensible product claim, not a marketing angle.

problems.title: How do homeowners verify carpenter work quality before payment?
problems.description: Customers commissioning custom furniture or carpentry work cannot verify quality standards before final payment. Defects like misaligned doors, poor finishing, or wrong measurements appear after installation. Carpenters demand full payment upon installation. Rework requests are denied or cost extra. No quality verification or milestone-based payment system exists.
problems.who: Homeowners commissioning wardrobes and modular furniture who pay before seeing defects.
problems.pitch: Milestone escrow and an inspection checklist for custom carpentry, with 10% held back until the fit is right.

how: Convert the design into measurable acceptance criteria: dimensions, alignment, finish, hardware and closing tolerance.
Release payment in three milestones, with photo and video inspection at each stage.
Hold 10% for 30 days and provide an independent inspector for disputed defects.
solution.model: 2–3% escrow fee plus inspection charges.
solution.gtm: Interior designers, modular kitchen showrooms and apartment handover communities.
solution.moat: Standardised acceptance criteria and inspector supply.

problems.verdict: Holdback is the cheapest quality assurance ever invented.

problems.title: Why do confirmed salon appointments still involve 30-minute waits?
problems.description: Despite booking confirmed appointment slots, salon customers routinely experience lengthy waiting periods because establishments rely on manual scheduling systems that don't account for service duration variability, stylist availability conflicts, or the cascading delays caused by earlier appointments running overtime.
problems.who: Salon customers who book a 6 pm slot and still wait 30 minutes; salon owners who lose walk-ins to unpredictable throughput.
problems.pitch: A live salon queue that tells you the real start time and pays you back when the chair runs late.

how: Instrument each chair with a lightweight tablet flow that timestamps service start and finish, building real throughput data.
Predict start times from the queue and service mix, then show customers a live 'you'll be seated at 6:12' status.
Auto-apply a credit when the predicted time slips beyond 10 minutes, funded from the salon's marketing budget.
solution.model: SaaS per chair with a performance fee tied to redeemed credits.
solution.gtm: Sell through salon equipment distributors and existing booking partners; lead with the queue, not the software.
solution.moat: Chair-level service-time data that improves prediction with every appointment.

market.tam: ₹9,000 Cr salon services; queue software a ₹400 Cr opportunity

problems.verdict: If you can predict the wait, you can sell the fix.

problems.title: Why can’t households easily access digital proof for in-warranty product repairs?
problems.description: Households lose hundreds to thousands annually on out-of-warranty repair charges for products still within coverage because they cannot find misplaced paper warranty cards or present faded thermal-paper receipts that have become illegible, leaving manufacturers and retailers to deny valid warranty claims.
problems.who: Households losing warranty claims because the bill faded or the card is missing.
problems.pitch: A warranty wallet that turns a photo of any bill into a retrievable, claimable product record.

how: Scan or forward invoices; OCR extracts product, serial number, purchase date and warranty terms into a searchable wallet.
Store service and repair records against each product, with reminders before warranty expiry.
Generate a claim pack (invoice, warranty, service history) and route it to the brand's service desk.
solution.model: Freemium consumer app; brand SaaS for claims processing; affiliate revenue on extended warranties and repairs.
solution.price: Free for 20 products; ₹499/year for unlimited; ₹15,000/month brand dashboard.
solution.gtm: App-store SEO on 'warranty tracker', partnerships with appliance brands and service aggregators.
solution.moat: A user's product and service graph plus brand integrations.

risks: Brands may not accept digital proof

market.tam: ₹3,000 Cr appliance service market; warranty leakage a measurable pain

problems.verdict: Own the proof and you own the repair moment.

problems.title: Why is there no reliable same-day personalized gifting for last-minute occasions?
problems.description: Busy professionals and forgetful individuals who suddenly remember birthdays or anniversaries at the last minute resort to generic, thoughtless gift purchases like cash, gift cards, or random store items because there is no curated, personalized, same-day gift delivery service that can save them from social embarrassment.
problems.who: Professionals who remember an anniversary at 4 pm and need to look thoughtful by 8 pm.
problems.pitch: A gifting concierge on WhatsApp that assembles a personalised gift from local inventory and delivers it in two hours.

how: Curate a local inventory of gifts, flowers, cakes and personalisation options with real-time stock from partner stores.
Take a short brief (relationship, budget, occasion) on WhatsApp and return three options in minutes.
Batch orders to nearby stores for two-hour delivery and add a handwritten note and photo proof.
solution.model: Product margin plus a concierge fee; corporate gifting contracts.
solution.gtm: Instagram ads around occasions, office admin networks, and calendar-reminder integrations.
solution.moat: Local inventory density and a concierge playbook that produces good taste at speed.

market.tam: ₹8,000 Cr gifting market; same-day personalised is a premium niche

problems.verdict: Sell the save, not the gift.

problems.title: Why is connecting specialized hardware to laptops still unreliable and frustrating?
problems.description: A driver CD from 2014, a forum thread, and a technician who knows the trick. Hardware vendors do not maintain drivers across OS versions, and IT teams have no device-level telemetry until something breaks.
problems.who: Labs, clinics, factory floors and field teams running legacy instruments on Windows, macOS and Linux.
problems.pitch: A compatibility cloud that makes specialized hardware plug-and-play with any laptop.

how: Build a compatibility database keyed by vendor and product ID, with signed driver packs and firmware versions.
Provide a virtual device lab so an IT team can test an OS update before it reaches the instrument.
Ship a small diagnostics agent and a support desk with an SLA for fleet customers.
mvp: Paid support desk for three lab customers
solution.model: Per-seat IT subscription, per-device fleet licensing, vendor certification fees.
solution.price: ₹2,999 per seat per year. Fleet plans from ₹1 lakh/year.
solution.gtm: Lab-equipment resellers, IT service providers and niche hardware vendors who want happier customers.
solution.moat: A proprietary compatibility graph and a physical test lab. Boring, deep and hard to replicate.

market.tam: Global instrument and industrial device support, with Indian labs and factories as the wedge

problems.verdict: Nobody wants to build driver infrastructure. That is exactly why the company that does becomes the default.

problems.title: Why do meetings waste 4 hours daily instead of summaries?
problems.description: Corporate employees spend half their workday in back-to-back status meetings, planning discussions, and review calls that could be replaced by brief written updates if they had AI-powered real-time meeting transcription and summarization tools optimized to understand Indian accents and business context.
problems.who: Teams losing half the day to status calls and rewriting notes afterwards.
problems.pitch: Meeting notes built for Indian accents and code-switching, with decisions and action items pushed to the tools teams already use.

how: Transcribe with accent- and code-switch-aware models, then extract decisions, owners and deadlines.
Push action items to Slack, Jira, Asana or WhatsApp, and draft the follow-up message.
Replace recurring status meetings with an async digest generated from the previous week's updates.
solution.model: Per-seat SaaS with a usage cap.
solution.gtm: Remote-first Indian startups, agencies and GCC teams.
solution.moat: Accent and code-switch training data plus workflow integrations.

problems.verdict: The note is not the product; the follow-through is.

problems.title: How can tourists find authentic experiences beyond major attractions?
problems.description: Tourists tired of visiting the same overcrowded landmark attractions mentioned in guidebooks want access to authentic local experiences, hidden neighborhood spots, and cultural activities but cannot easily connect with knowledgeable local insiders who can curate personalized off-the-beaten-path itineraries matched to interests.
problems.who: Travellers tired of the same five landmarks and the same guidebook.
problems.pitch: Verified local insiders who design a half-day route around your interests — not a group tour bus.

how: Recruit and interview locals with deep neighbourhood knowledge, then certify them on safety and storytelling.
Match by interest — food, craft, music, architecture — and co-create a route with fixed pricing and a meeting point.
Add a post-experience review and a curated 'locals' shortlist' for each city.
solution.model: 20% commission on experiences; corporate offsite bookings.
solution.gtm: Boutique hotels, travel creators and city tourism boards.
solution.moat: Vetted local supply and route quality.

problems.verdict: Authenticity scales through people, not inventory.

problems.title: Why is foreign transaction pricing still confusing for consumers?
problems.description: Travelers using forex cards for international payments discover they're paying 3-5% more than advertised exchange rates through hidden markups and transaction fees. Card companies advertise 'zero markup' but add charges in fine print. Comparing actual costs across forex cards, credit cards, and cash withdrawal is complex. Users cannot calculate true cost of foreign transactions before travel.
problems.who: Travellers paying 3–5% more than the advertised rate on forex cards.
problems.pitch: The real cost of spending abroad — card markup, ATM fees and FX spread — before you leave home.

how: Model the all-in cost of each card, forex card and cash channel using live rates plus issuer markups and fees.
Let travellers simulate their itinerary spend and see which combination is cheapest.
Track actual transactions against the estimate and flag overcharges for dispute.
solution.model: Card referral commissions and a premium trip plan.
solution.gtm: Travel creators, visa agencies and international student groups.
solution.moat: Issuer fee data and real transaction benchmarks.

problems.verdict: Zero markup is a story; the all-in cost is the truth.

problems.title: How do customers find water tank cleaning services?
problems.description: Apartment residents needing annual water tank cleaning struggle finding professional services. Most plumbers don't offer tank cleaning. Finding specialized agencies requires word-of-mouth. Pricing isn't transparent (₹1,500-5,000 per tank). Scheduling is difficult. No verified water tank cleaning platform exists with health certification.
problems.who: Apartment societies and villas that cannot find a specialist and have no proof of cleanliness.
problems.pitch: Verified water-tank cleaning with before/after photos, a potability test and a health certificate per tank.

how: Build a four-step protocol: drain, scrub, disinfect, refill, with photo documentation at each stage.
Take a water sample after refill and issue a potability certificate within 48 hours.
Schedule annual cleaning with reminders and society-level compliance records.
solution.model: Per-tank fee plus an annual society contract.
solution.gtm: Society committees, facility managers and municipal health campaigns.
solution.moat: Society contracts and a compliance record that committees can show residents.

problems.verdict: A certificate turns an invisible chore into a trust asset.

problems.title: Why don't salon bookings guarantee your preferred stylist?
problems.description: Customers booking salon appointments find themselves assigned to random available staff members rather than their preferred skilled stylist, resulting in inconsistent haircut quality, miscommunication about desired styles, and repeated disappointments that erode trust in salon booking systems.
problems.who: Salon customers who keep getting reassigned, and salon owners losing regulars to inconsistent service.
problems.pitch: Booking software that only sells a slot when the requested stylist can actually deliver it — with duration-aware buffers and a late-start guarantee.

how: Model each service's real duration distribution per stylist, then block calendar time from the actual p90 rather than the menu estimate.
Expose stylist-specific booking pages and hold a 10-minute buffer after overrun-prone services.
Publish a live queue to the customer and auto-issue a credit if the chair is more than 10 minutes late.
mvp: Customer booking page with stylist lock
solution.model: ₹2,500–₹6,000 monthly SaaS per salon plus a small per-booking fee on prepaid appointments.
solution.gtm: Start with 25 independent salons in one city; use the customer-facing guarantee as the wedge against generic booking apps.
solution.moat: Per-stylist duration data and switching costs once the salon's calendar and clients live here.

market.tam: ₹9,000 Cr salon services; scheduling software is a ₹600 Cr wedge

problems.verdict: The broken promise is a data problem — sell the guarantee, not the calendar.

problems.title: How can kirana stores predict restocking needs using past sales data?
problems.description: Small retail kirana stores managing hundreds of SKUs rely on guesswork to reorder inventory, frequently running out of fast-moving items or over-stocking slow sellers because they lack affordable AI-powered predictive analytics that can forecast demand patterns based on historical sales data and seasonal trends.
problems.who: Kirana owners guessing which of 800 SKUs to reorder before a festival or a heatwave.
problems.pitch: Demand forecasts and reorder suggestions for kirana stores, built from the billing data they already generate.

how: Connect to the store's billing software or upload daily sales, then forecast SKU demand by weekday, season and festival.
Generate an order sheet with suggested quantities and a WhatsApp order to the distributor.
Flag slow movers and expiring stock with a discount suggestion.
solution.model: ₹499–₹999/month per store plus a distributor referral fee.
solution.gtm: Billing-software partnerships and FMCG distributor networks.
solution.moat: Store-level demand data and distributor relationships.

market.tam: ₹12 lakh kirana stores; retail analytics a ₹2,000 Cr opportunity

problems.verdict: The billing machine already knows; the owner just cannot hear it.

problems.title: Why doesn’t on-demand arborist tech exist for emergency tree risk mitigation?
problems.description: Residents requesting municipal tree pruning of dangerous overhanging branches threatening power lines or buildings face 6-12 month delays. No emergency arborist services exist. Monsoon damage risks increase due to bureaucratic processes.
problems.who: Residents and societies with branches over power lines and a municipality that takes a year.
problems.pitch: Certified arborists on demand for hazardous trees, with a risk assessment and a pruning plan before monsoon.

how: Certify arborists on a risk-scoring protocol (species, lean, cracks, proximity to infrastructure).
Dispatch a crew with insurance and a written pruning plan; coordinate with the local utility for power-line work.
Run pre-monsoon assessment camps for societies and publish a tree-risk map.
solution.model: Per-assessment and pruning fee; annual society contracts.
solution.gtm: Housing societies, utilities and municipal parks departments.
solution.moat: Certified arborist supply and risk data.

problems.verdict: A falling branch is an emergency; pruning it is a scheduled service.

problems.title: Why do home deep cleaning services lack quality standards?
problems.description: Customers hiring deep cleaning services for ₹3,000-8,000 experience inconsistent quality - some areas are cleaned well while others are missed. No checklists or quality verification exists. Customers cannot track cleaner background or reviews. Payment is expected regardless of satisfaction. Standardized deep cleaning protocols don't exist.
problems.who: Customers paying ₹6,000 and finding the kitchen chimney still greasy.
problems.pitch: A room-by-room deep-clean checklist with photo proof per zone and 15% payment held until you sign off.

how: Break the job into 60 verifiable checkpoints across kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms and balcony.
Require the crew to photograph each checkpoint in-app; the customer reviews before payment release.
Hold 15% for 48 hours and send a re-clean crew for any failed checkpoint.
solution.model: Booking commission plus a crew SaaS fee.
solution.gtm: Apartment deep-clean cycles before festivals, plus real-estate handover partnerships.
solution.moat: Checkpoint standards and crew compliance data.

problems.verdict: Define clean, or the customer will define it for you.

problems.title: Where can working women find on-call saree draping professionals?
problems.description: Urban professional women attending traditional weddings, office functions, or morning ceremonies cannot easily locate and book skilled saree draping experts on short notice who can arrive at their homes early to help them dress appropriately and elegantly for time-sensitive events.
problems.who: Working women with 7–10 am functions, weddings and office ethnic days who need a skilled draper at short notice.
problems.pitch: On-demand saree draping at home in 60 minutes, with a fixed menu of drape styles and morning slots that actually exist.

how: Recruit and train drapers on a standard style menu (Nivi, dhoti, lehenga-drape, mumty) with a 45-minute service-level target.
Offer pre-booked early-morning slots and a 90-minute express window priced separately, with live draper tracking.
Add a pin-and-finish guarantee: if the drape slips within four hours, a draper returns free.
mvp: WhatsApp booking with four fixed drape styles and slot inventory
Style guide cards the customer keeps
solution.model: Per-visit fee plus a monthly 'event wardrobe' pass; stylist supply is gig-based.
solution.price: ₹499–₹899 per drape; ₹199 extra for pre-7 am; ₹1,999 for a five-event pass.
solution.gtm: Partner with salon chains, bridal boutiques and office women's networks; rank on 'saree draping near me'.
solution.moat: Trained draper density per zone and a reliability score that is hard to replicate quickly.

market.tam: ₹1,800 Cr unorganised saree-draping and event-grooming services

problems.verdict: A narrow, recurring need with almost no organised supply — density is the whole game.

problems.title: Where can men find affordable specialized beard grooming services?
problems.description: Men seeking professional beard trimming, shaping, and grooming services find limited options beyond overpriced upscale grooming lounges, as neighborhood barbershops typically lack the specialized training, tools, and products needed to create and maintain modern beard styles and designs.
problems.who: Men aged 22–40 who want shape, fade and beard design without upscale lounge prices.
problems.pitch: A standardised beard-grooming service inside existing barbershops — trained staff, modern tool kits and a fixed price menu.

how: Train neighbourhood barbers on six beard styles with a tool kit, sanitation protocol and 30-minute service standard.
List certified shops with transparent prices and before/after photos; let customers book a specific barber.
Sell a monthly grooming membership that works across partner shops.
solution.model: Certification fees, product kit sales, and a share of membership revenue.
solution.price: ₹249–₹499 per service; ₹799 monthly membership for two visits.
solution.gtm: Hyperlocal Instagram before/after content and shop-front co-branding; expand shop-by-shop in dense clusters.
solution.moat: A trained barber network and a recognisable service standard inside existing real estate.

problems.verdict: Asset-light standardisation beats building premium lounges.

problems.title: Where can DIY skincare makers source lab-grade raw ingredients?
problems.description: Home beauty product makers and natural skincare experimenters cannot easily purchase high-quality raw materials like cosmetic-grade clays, essential oils, botanical extracts, and specialty ingredients in small consumer-friendly quantities from trusted suppliers who can verify purity and provide safety data sheets.
problems.who: Home skincare makers and small indie brands who cannot meet supplier minimums or verify purity.
problems.pitch: A certified small-quantity marketplace for cosmetic ingredients, with COAs, safety data sheets and formulation recipes.

how: Stock 150 cosmetic-grade ingredients in 50g–1kg packs with batch-linked COA and SDS documents.
Publish tested starter formulas with percentages and stability notes, so buyers can actually use what they purchase.
Add a lab-testing add-on for indie brands that need microbial and heavy-metal reports.
solution.model: Product margin, testing fees, and a paid formulator community.
solution.gtm: SEO on ingredient + formulation queries, DIY skincare creators, and Instagram education.
solution.moat: Supplier relationships, batch documentation and a trusted formulation library.

market.tam: ₹1,200 Cr indie beauty inputs and DIY segment

problems.verdict: Trust documentation is the product; the ingredients are the attach.

problems.title: Why is finding affordable mehendi artists so difficult for small home celebrations?
problems.description: Families hosting intimate celebrations and small home gatherings struggle to find talented mehendi/henna artists available for modest events because most professionals are either booked for large weddings or charge the same premium "wedding season" rates regardless of event size or complexity.
problems.who: Families hosting 10–40 guest gatherings — engagements, poojas, baby showers — who cannot justify wedding-rate artists.
problems.pitch: Fixed-price mehendi artists for small home celebrations, priced by design complexity instead of wedding-season hype.

how: Publish a five-tier design menu with fixed prices and time estimates, so a small function can book without negotiation.
Recruit part-time artists and fill their weekday and afternoon capacity with small-event demand.
Add a henna-paste quality check and a patch test, plus a photo proof of the finished design.
mvp: Prepaid booking with a 2-hour arrival window
solution.model: 20% commission on bookings; artist training and starter-kit sales.
solution.price: ₹1,200 for four hands (simple) to ₹6,500 for bridal-style; ₹299 per extra guest.
solution.gtm: Instagram design gallery, society WhatsApp groups, and partnerships with small-event decorators and caterers.
solution.moat: A price-menu brand and artist utilisation data in off-peak slots.

problems.verdict: Small celebrations are underserved because the industry only prices for weddings.
